feda9361cf1f.title: discussion — settling what an agent cannot read off disk
feda9361cf1f.content: Skill discussion: Settle which harness, and which repositories, when no file says: the output is a document conforming to discussion.output.schema.json. Named by: Complete initialization, Determine the harness and repositories, Initialize a harness . An agent that has just read bootstrap’s README.md knows the shape of a harness and nothing about this one. Two questions have no answer in any file it can reach: . | which harness this repository should become: bootstrap itself, or any Harness built on it; | which repositories are involved — where the dependency is read from, where the new declaration is written to, and whether they are the same. | . Only whoever asked for the harness can answer them, so the agent asks. This skill says what the asking must produce. processes/discussion.bpmn narrows the candidates and then calls human-agent-discussion, the one reusable way bootstrap asks a person anything, with no default allowed.

7782afb8a922.title: Inputs and outputs
7782afb8a922.content: |   |   | . | in | discussion.input.schema.json: what the agent already knows, and which of the two unknowns is open | . | out | discussion.output.schema.json: harness, repositories[], outcome, determinedBy, answeredBy, and the exchange that produced it | . Both are plain JSON Schema in schemas/, readable with nothing installed. The task is finished when a document conforming to the output schema exists, not when a conversation has taken place. The participant may be a person or a sibling agent that already holds the answer; the output records which (kind: person | agent), as human-agent-discussion says.

c8f2570c7cb0.title: First, say where you are
c8f2570c7cb0.content: Before narrowing anything (A_DetermineWhere), determine the three things human-agent-discussion requires before any question: . | the Process: Initialize a harness, inside Determine the harness and repositories. A Bootstrapping Agent can be nowhere else (FR-2); | the Roles: itself as the Bootstrapping Agent; the person it will ask as the Requestor. A request relayed by somebody else leaves the Requestor undetermined; | the context: what the request said, and what the checkout holds. | . One that cannot be determined is never filled with a default: it is asked about first, and the harness question waits.

6a10eef7b1f7.title: Rules
6a10eef7b1f7.content: Ask the fewest questions that settle it. Narrow the candidate list from context first (a repository whose root already holds a declaration, <name>.json, is not a blank slate) and put the rest as one question with the candidates named. A question a reader must go and research is not ready. Never infer the answer from a default. If nothing is known, the output’s determinedBy is asked, not assumed. assumed is permitted only for a default the README states, and assumption then names it. Record repositories as pairs, not as a list. read from and written to can be the same repository or two; the point of determining them is to know where the declaration lands. Never infer written-to from push access. A remote repository is read-from until the Requestor authorizes writing to it (confirm-harness). A refusal is an outcome. If the participant declines, that is outcome: "unsettled" with what was asked and what is still open — not a guess, and not an error.

0acc32e92764.title: /dispatch-agent — parallel dispatch with a live 2-minute status heartbeat
0acc32e92764.content: Skill dispatch-agent: Dispatch one or more background sub-agents against parallel research/build fronts with a STANDARDIZED live progress contract, and monitor them on a 2-minute heartbeat. Every dispatched agent emits consistent DID/DOING/NEXT/BLOCKERS blocks with real log output (not static “still running”); the parent extracts the latest block from each agent every ~120 s and posts one consolidated synthesis table. Use when the user says “dispatch agents”, “fan out”, “run these in parallel with monitoring”, “give me status every 2 minutes”, or when you are about to launch ≥ 2 background Agents on independent work. Named by: Content acquisition, Copy out materialized content — to work on somebody else’s bytes, Basic ingestion — an upload to an asset catalogued in library/, Materialize remote content: the shared subprocess, Adopt a methodology from a source document, Multi-locale translation, Refresh materialized remote content, Sample import into a structured data store, Subscribe to an external knowledge graph, Related work: find, sort, summarize, ask to coordinate, Secure agent permissions, Session state machine, Board: open and close content, Board: relocate content to the trashcan . The expensive failure mode of multi-agent dispatch is going dark: you launch N background agents, then can’t say what any of them is doing until it completes 20 minutes later. This skill fixes that with two halves that MUST be used together: . | Agent-side progress contract — every dispatched agent emits a consistent, machine-greppable progress block on a fixed cadence, with live evidence (log tails, exit codes, counts), never a static “still working on it”. | Parent-side 2-minute heartbeat — the parent extracts the latest block from each running agent every ~120 s and posts ONE consolidated synthesis table to the user, so monitoring is passive and effortless. | . Both halves are load-bearing. An agent that doesn’t follow the contract can’t be synthesized; a parent that doesn’t run the heartbeat leaves the user blind. Do not dispatch without both.

19b971dc9454.title: 0a. Interactive child session vs background agent — choose FIRST (owner directive 2026-11-25, STRICT)
19b971dc9454.content: Owner, verbatim: “If you are swarming a process around research that might require interaction with the author or owner then that should be a proper child sibling that is interactive not a spawning process that you can’t engage in. … This should be a general practice unless it’s known that the swarm activities very mechanical and does not need any human attraction.” . A background Agent (this skill’s default) cannot be steered: the owner cannot see it, talk to it, or answer its questions. So before dispatching, classify each front: . | front | how to launch | . | Research / derivation / open question — a route choice, a modelling or convention choice, a definition the corpus leaves open, anything whose next step may need the owner | Interactive child session: mcp__claude-code-remote__create_session (with source_url of the repo and a self-contained prompt). It appears in the owner’s session list; the owner can read and steer it, and it asks the owner directly (AskUserQuestion, chat-mirrored). Tell it to send progress to the parent with send_message. | . | Mechanical — a known procedure with one right answer: re-run a producer, attribute a measured change, refresh witnesses, apply a ruled fix, a lint/audit drain | Background Agent is fine. Any owner decision it surfaces is framed in its report and relayed by the parent. | . | Unsure | Treat as research → interactive child session. | . Rules for an interactive research child: . | Its prompt must say it is interactive, must ask the owner at forks rather than guess, and must post its pre-registered plan to the owner before computing. | It inherits every repository discipline (anti-fit, NO-FLOAT64, Strict Lean, no lake build, fences); put the essentials in the prompt, because it starts with no context. | The parent records the child’s session id on the bean and in its progress report, so the owner can find it. | If a background agent turns out to need owner input, stop it, check its worktree for unpushed work, and relaunch the front as an interactive child session with that context. | .

6987ccc3c938.title: 0. When to use
6987ccc3c938.content: . | Launching ≥ 2 background Agent calls on independent fronts (research routes, per-file proofs, per-isotope compute). | The user asks for periodic status (“update me every 2 minutes”, “keep me posted”, “monitor these”). | A single long agent whose progress the user wants to watch live. | . For a single quick synchronous agent whose result you need before the next step, skip this — just call Agent(run_in_background: false).

ac36962969f4.title: 1. Agent-side progress contract (PASTE THIS into every dispatched agent)
ac36962969f4.content: Append the block below verbatim to every agent prompt you dispatch through this skill. Fill in <LABEL> with a short stable tag (≤ 16 chars, kebab-case: a3-offblock, ctil-root, a4-interface) — the parent keys the synthesis table on it. ## PROGRESS REPORTING CONTRACT (STRICT — the parent monitors you on this) Your label is: <LABEL> Emit a progress block **as a plain-text assistant message** (not a tool call) at EVERY meaningful step, and **at least once every ~90 seconds of wall time** even mid-step. Use this EXACT shape so the parent can grep and synthesize it: ### ⟦PROGRESS⟧ <LABEL> · step N DID: <what you just finished — CONCRETE evidence only: file paths, lean exit codes, real-sorry counts, git shas, row counts, the tail of a log. NOT "worked on the proof".> DOING: <the step in flight right now. If a command is RUNNING, quote the last 3–8 relevant lines of its output / the key live metric (elapsed, % done, current goal state, error so far). NEVER a canned "still running" — show the live log.> NEXT: <the single concrete next action you will take.> BLOCKERS: <none | the precise blocker (missing lemma name, 403, ENOSPC, evicted oleans, ambiguous spec).> Rules that keep updates LIVE, not semi-static: - **Tee every long command to a log and quote its tail** in DOING: `<cmd> 2>&1 | tee /tmp/<LABEL>-<step>.log` then put the last lines in the block. A Lean check, a python compute, a git op > ~10 s all qualify. - **Advance the step counter** every block; never repeat an identical block twice — if nothing changed, say what you are still waiting on and quote the newest log line. - **Evidence or it didn't happen**: every DID line names a file / exit code / count / sha. No vague verbs. - When you finish, emit a final block with marker `### ⟦DONE⟧ <LABEL>` carrying the verdict (closed / scope-(a) / scope-(b) / bean-the-gap), the exact .lean path(s), lean-direct exit code, real-sorry count, and the branch you pushed. Why this exact shape: the parent’s extractor (below) greps for the ⟦PROGRESS⟧ / ⟦DONE⟧ markers and pulls the DID/DOING/NEXT/BLOCKERS lines. Consistent markers → one-line-per-agent synthesis with zero guessing. Deviating from the marker or the four keys breaks the monitor. This contract is additive to the task’s own discipline (anti-fit, lean-direct verification, zero-sorry, bean-the-gap). It governs how the agent reports, never what counts as done. An agent still may not launder a fit or fake a closure to make its DID line look better — honesty over a pretty status.

9c81006c4c88.title: 2. Dispatch procedure
9c81006c4c88.content: . | Scope each front to one independent agent (no shared files between agents — worktree isolation makes parallel file writes safe; use isolation: "worktree" whenever agents mutate the tree). | Assign each a <LABEL> and paste both: . | the §1 progress contract block above, AND | the Mandatory Sibling Launch Briefing from swarm-sibling-launch.md (Template A for the single merge-steward, Template B for every Coding / Proof / Prose / Compute Sibling — injecting .claude/skills/local/*.md, continual-progress.md, idle-backlog.md, merge-queue.md sibling-side submission with zero self-merging, one-voice external-reader hygiene, two-step witness SHA stamping, reverting the 9 qou-v0t8 contended audit witnesses, CPU throttling, and branch/public-release fences). | . | Launch all agents in a single message (multiple Agent tool calls) so they run concurrently. Record each returned agentId ↔ <LABEL> mapping in a scratch note (/tmp/<session>-dispatch-map.txt) so the heartbeat can label rows even before an agent’s first block lands. | Immediately arm the heartbeat (§3). Do not end the turn without it. | .

07ae73e86a88.title: 3. Parent-side 2-minute heartbeat
07ae73e86a88.content: 3a. The extractor (targeted — never read the full JSONL) . Reading an agent’s whole *.output transcript overflows context. Extract ONLY the latest progress block per agent. Save this once as scripts/agent-progress.py (or inline it): . #!/usr/bin/env python3 # Usage: agent-progress.py <tasks-dir> # Prints the latest ⟦PROGRESS⟧/⟦DONE⟧ block from each agent's *.output JSONL. import json, re, sys, glob, os tasks = sys.argv[1] for f in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(tasks, "*.output"))): aid = os.path.basename(f)[:-7] last = None try: for line in open(f): try: o = json.loads(line) except Exception: continue for c in (o.get("message", {}).get("content") or []): if isinstance(c, dict) and c.get("type") == "text": t = c.get("text", "") if "⟦PROGRESS⟧" in t or "⟦DONE⟧" in t: # keep only from the last marker onward idx = max(t.rfind("⟦PROGRESS⟧"), t.rfind("⟦DONE⟧")) last = t[t.rfind("###", 0, idx):] if idx >= 0 else t except FileNotFoundError: continue done = last and "⟦DONE⟧" in last print(f"===== {aid[:12]} {'[DONE]' if done else '[live]'} =====") print((last or "(no progress block yet — agent still spinning up)").strip()[:900]) print() . Run it against the session tasks dir: python3 scripts/agent-progress.py "$TASKS_DIR" where $TASKS_DIR is the tasks/ folder holding the <agentId>.output files (the dispatch tool result names each output_file; its parent dir is $TASKS_DIR). 🛑 That dir also holds the stdout of every BACKGROUNDED BASH JOB, and a glob cannot tell them apart by name. Measured 2026-10-10: a heartbeat over a dir with one agent and six backgrounded Bash commands printed seven rows, six reading [live] (no progress block yet — agent still spinning up) — for a pip install, a setup-folio-assistant.sh and a precision-gates.sh run. They never advance, because a Bash job emits no ⟦PROGRESS⟧ block, so they read as permanently-hung agents and invite a SendMessage nudge to something that cannot receive one. And it buried a real signal: one of the six had TIMED OUT (GATE_EXIT=124) while its row said “spinning up”. scripts/agent-progress.py now discriminates on the first line — an agent transcript is JSONL whose first record carries isSidechain/parentUuid/promptId; Bash stdout is arbitrary text — and announces the count it skipped rather than filtering silently. Same dir, after the fix: (skipped 7 non-agent .output file(s)) then one row. Two consequences for the heartbeat. A [live] row with no block is only evidence about an agent if the file is an agent transcript — check before nudging. And cat the Bash job’s own .output when you want its result; the extractor deliberately will not show it, and a 0-byte file under a | tail pipeline means “not finished”, not “crashed”. 3b. The cadence . Every ~120 s while any agent is still [live]: . | Run the extractor. | Post ONE consolidated synthesis to the user — a compact table, one row per agent, newest block only: . | label | DID (evidence) | DOING (live) | NEXT | BLOCKERS |——-|—————-|————–|——|———-| . Keep it to one screen. If a block is stale (same step counter as last heartbeat and > 3 min old), flag it ⚠ stale and note you’ll SendMessage the agent to nudge it. | Re-arm the next 120 s tick, then end the turn (do not busy-wait). | . Cadence mechanism — do NOT foreground-sleep (blocked). Use one of: . | ScheduleWakeup with delaySeconds: 120, prompt: "/dispatch-agent heartbeat", reason: "2-min agent status heartbeat" — the standard dynamic-loop tick. Call ScheduleWakeup({stop:true}) once every agent is [DONE]. | If the harness surfaces agent-completion notifications, those also wake you; run the extractor on each and treat it as an off-cadence heartbeat, then re-arm the 120 s fallback so quiet stretches still tick. | . The 120 s tick is a fallback heartbeat, not the only signal — completion notifications arrive on their own. Pick 120 s because the user asked for 2-minute updates; honor that literally. 3c. Nudging a silent agent . If an agent shows (no progress block yet) for > 3 min, or its step counter hasn’t advanced across two heartbeats, `SendMessage(to: . , ...)` with a one-line nudge: *"Emit a fresh ⟦PROGRESS⟧ block with the live tail of whatever is running."* An agent that has genuinely hung (evicted oleans, ENOSPC) will surface it as a BLOCKER once nudged. --- ## 4. On completion When an agent emits `⟦DONE⟧` (or the harness notifies completion): 1. Drop it from the `[live]` set; keep its final block in the synthesis as a `[DONE]` row. 2. **Verify before trusting the DONE line.** The agent's self-reported "sorry-free / exit 0" is a claim — the parent re-runs lean-direct on each edited `.lean` itself (exit 0, no `declaration uses 'sorry'`) before merging, exactly as for any dispatched Lean work. A green DID line never substitutes for the parent's own verification. 3. When **all** agents are `[DONE]`: post a final consolidated synthesis (verdict per front + the merge/next-step queue), `ScheduleWakeup( {stop:true})`, and end the heartbeat. --- ## 5. Anti-patterns (each is a skill violation) - **Going dark** — dispatching background agents without arming the heartbeat. The user then has to ask "what's happening?" — the exact friction this skill removes. - **Semi-static updates** — "agent still running the proof" with no log tail, no step counter, no evidence. If a command is in flight, the block MUST carry its live output. - **Reading the full transcript** — tailing/`cat`-ing the `*.output` JSONL into context instead of using the targeted extractor. Overflows context and defeats the point. - **Trusting the DONE line** — merging on an agent's self-reported "exit 0" without the parent's own lean-direct re-verification. - **Wrong cadence** — 5-minute or "when I remember" ticks when the user asked for 2 minutes. Honor the literal cadence.

edbce3cbddfc.title: A computed gateway is not a chosen one
edbce3cbddfc.content: In this repository a DMN table has a second job: an exclusive gateway carrying <cat-harness.processes:decision ref="decisions/<file>.dmn#<Decision_Id>"/> has its branch computed from the table rather than picked by the agent. workflow_complete refuses a hand-supplied outcome at such a gateway. Asserting the answer would defeat the point of writing the table. You pass facts — e.g. { failCritical: 0, failMajor: 2 } from qa_sweep totals — and the table returns the branch. Adding one means adding the .dmn, the cat-harness.processes:decision ref, and nothing else: the loader checks that every outcome the table can return names a real outgoing flow, so a table that can route somewhere the diagram cannot go is a load error rather than a surprise at the moment of decision.

a8eb335eb71f.title: The FEEL subset this interpreter implements
a8eb335eb71f.content: src/workflow/decision-table.ts implements a deliberate subset: - (any), literals, comparisons, and one-of. It refuses ranges, not() and function calls rather than mis-evaluating them. Write within that subset: a table using a construct the interpreter rejects fails at load, rather than being mis-evaluated at the moment of decision.

34acb4c3a308.title: Three states belong in the table
34acb4c3a308.content: Encode “could not determine” as an outcome in its own right — pages-live-gate.dmn returns live, not-yet and unknown; folio-intent.dmn returns ask when the filesystem cannot decide. A gate whose only outcomes are pass and fail forces an unmeasured input to be rendered as one of them, and it is always rendered as pass. If your decision has an input that may be unavailable, give it a branch.

ff4b0b5cb4e0.title: Hit policy
ff4b0b5cb4e0.content: Say it explicitly. FIRST is the usual choice here and is what folio-intent.dmn uses — rules are ordered, the first match wins, and the ordering is then part of the logic and must be reviewed as such.

2d84c9344a2b.title: When a layer above transforms it
2d84c9344a2b.content: A layer built on this one may render decision tables for human review or derive other artefacts (questionnaires, for instance) from them. Then the DMN is a source artefact, not documentation of one; that layer’s own tooling skill has the mechanics and the caveats, and this one names no layer above it.

8fe43fa4a3f1.doc: Basic ingestion — an upload to an asset catalogued in library/
8fe43fa4a3f1.title: Basic ingestion — an upload to an asset catalogued in library/
8fe43fa4a3f1.content: Process_Ingestion · advisory · 4 step(s) . Accepts an upload, records its extracted metadata in the knowledge graph, and catalogues the asset in library/ — held if materialized, referenced if not. THE BASIC FLOW, with very little process context assumed. Accept, extract the metadata into the KG, ask whether the asset is materialized, place it in library/<slug>/. It calls NO subprocess and makes no content-type decision. THE ID Process_Ingestion IS KEPT ON PURPOSE: methodology-from-source.bpmn’s Call_Ingest names it, and so does every higher-layer process that refines this flow. Refinement is by INVERSION — a refining process calls this one as its first step and continues with its own work; nothing here names a refinement, because the corpus has no BPMN extension point and a harness diagram naming a higher one would be an upward edge. The document pipeline (rungs, the four ingest phases, the L1 completeness gate, promotion, the summary queue) is such a refinement, in the layer above. i i i i Actors: Contributor (human or agent) · Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) .

7d5b95efcf91.doc: Basic ingestion — an upload to an asset catalogued in library/
7d5b95efcf91.title: Lanes — who acts
7d5b95efcf91.content: | lane | role | what it does here | . | Contributor (human or agent) | user | Whoever puts the file in the queue.“HUMAN OR AGENT” IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A HEDGE: both place files here. That is why Task_Place is a plain bpmn:task rather than a userTask — asserting a human performs it would contradict the lane’s own role graph, which is what activity-fulfilment-kind exists to catch.WHAT THE LANE IS ACCOUNTABLE FOR, and where it ends. Choosing a route, writing the bytes into the DECLARED queue of the layer that will own them, and discharging afterwards whatever that route could not — the web form has no working tree, so no pre-commit hook and no generator runs on it. The lane does NOT ingest and does not clean the queue: it hands over, and Lane_1 takes it from there. upload-routes carries the routes and their obligations. | . | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | ingestion-agent | Runs the basic flow from the metadata step to the placement in library/, unattended: every decision in it is decidable from the material and its declarations. It asks one question — is the asset materialized? — and that is answered from the materialization state vocabulary (schemas/kg/materialization-state.ts), not by judgement. It does NOT choose a reader for the bytes, derive sections or blocks, or describe images: those are a refining process’s work, which calls this flow first.THE FLOW ENDS IN THIS LANE. The asset catalogued in library/ — held, or recorded as referenced — is the terminal state, and every knowledge-graph reference to it resolves through library/ from here; a refining process continues from it rather than being drawn into this one. There is no separate corpus lane: it would hold only the end event, and a lane with no activity has no performer to describe. | .

abcda0459041.doc: Basic ingestion — an upload to an asset catalogued in library/
abcda0459041.title: Steps
abcda0459041.content: Every one of the 4 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | Place it in uploads/ by a declared routeTask_Place | Contributor (human or agent) | upload-routes | THE FIRST LINK: everything downstream of here takes a file that is already in the queue, so without this step how the file got there is governed by nothing.WHAT THIS STEP IS. The basic flow’s ACCEPT step: choosing an arrival route, writing the bytes into the declared queue of the layer that will own them, and discharging what that route does not discharge for you. The routes, what each writer owes, and the two that are mechanisms against the one that is a persona are in the upload-routes skill; upload-url composes the forge URL for the web route from the declaration rather than from a literal, because a hand-written one can 404.WHY A PLAIN bpmn:task AND NOT A userTask. A userTask asserts a human performs it, and this lane is “Contributor (human or agent)” because both do; asserting human-only would be an activity-fulfilment-kind contradiction. A plain task asserts nothing about the performer.WHY THE BEAN OP IS note AND NOT claim. Placing a file claims nothing; it adds to a queue. What it owes the work plan is visibility. A note against the ingestion bean is what makes the queue’s growth something another session can see. | . | Extract its metadata into the KGTask_ExtractMetadata | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | asset-extraction | THE METADATA STEP. What enters the knowledge graph is the asset’s INDEX — what it is, how big, what type, when it says it was written — and, for a container, what is in it; its contents do not go in unless somebody asks, with a reason. The tool is cat-harness-tools/scripts/extract-assets.ts, writing a folio-extraction/v1 record (schemas/content/extraction.ts).The media type is sniffed from the leading bytes, never taken from the extension. | . | **Place the asset in library//**`Task_PlaceInLibrary` | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | library-ingestion | The materialized branch. The asset lands in library/<slug>/ with its metadata record, its provenance and its fixity. The folder name IS the citation key, so a citation and a directory are the same string.The upload is then RETIRED, not left and not deleted: it moves to fsh-guts/uploads/ beside a sidecar naming where it came from and when, and check:uploads-retired finds one that was not. A refining process that derives content from the bytes does so before that retirement; library-ingestion carries the rule. | . | Record it in library/ as referencedTask_CatalogueReference | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | library-ingestion | The referenced branch. Nothing is fetched and no bytes are written: the catalogue record says where the asset is and that we hold none. A reference is not a fetch — it stays navigable without being held, and materializing it later is materialize-remote.bpmn’s decision, with its purpose and five gates, not this flow’s. | .

4f46175985b5.title: Decisions
4f46175985b5.content: Every one of the 1 decision(s) is documented. | decision | what decides it | branches | . | Materialized?Gateway_Materialized | Answered from the materialization state (schemas/kg/materialization-state.ts): materialized means the bytes are here; referenced means we know where they are and hold none. unknown is not a third branch here because a node must DECLARE its state — there is no default — and an asset this flow cannot classify is recorded as referenced-with-a-reason rather than placed as if held. Collapsing referenced into materialized is the failure the vocabulary exists to stop: corpus-grep searches library/ only, so a referenced node placed as held reads as present to every consumer. | materialized → Place the asset in library//**referenced** → Record it in library/ as referenced | .

3eaacfb5f63a.title: Document Intake
3eaacfb5f63a.content: Skill document-intake: Process uploaded documents (PDFs, scans, LaTeX, WHO L1/L2 guidelines, etc.) from library/ into structured content objects. Handles OCR extraction, environment detection, structural analysis, and content-object generation. Supports multi-stage pipelines: raw upload → extracted text → structured blocks → .ts/.md content objects. Named by: Ingestion subprocess — build the L1 knowledge graph, Ingestion subprocess — derive content from the assets, Ingestion subprocess — extract structure, Ingestion subprocess — the L1 completeness gate . Bib human-review integration (2026-06-09). Track per-upload ingestion status in library/intake.json (identified passage, formalised?, matched?) and link each upload to the references.ts entry it sources. An upload that supplies a cited source moves that ref to source-in-repo (agent-identified passage; no human photo) and then through the local/bib-human-review ladder to validated. Existing library/ follow the same agent-sourced path (design §5). Per-upload state now lives in the source ledger (2026-08-08). The library/<id>/intake.json convention below covers 1 of the corpus’s 284 documents; the per-document row — reference join, examination status, and relevance verdict — is now the source ledger (source-ledger/v1, now test/attestations/bib-verification/), populated by local/paper-relevance-triage. Use the ledger for “what is this document, is it cited, does it matter”; keep intake.json for the multi-stage extraction state of a document actually being converted (OCR → blocks → content objects). Do not record a title, author, or year in the ledger — bibliographic metadata belongs in folio/schema/references.ts alone.

c8c22fc10f69.title: Overview
c8c22fc10f69.content: This skill manages the library/ directory as an intake pipeline for converting raw documents into structured content objects. It handles: . | Scanned PDFs / images — OCR extraction → text → blocks | LaTeX source — environment extraction → blocks | WHO L1 → L2 guidelines — normative structure → blocks | arXiv papers — fetched source → blocks (delegates to paper-importer) | Arbitrary documents — best-effort structural analysis | . The key distinction from paper-importer: this skill owns the full lifecycle of library/, including tracking processing state, partial extractions, and multi-pass refinement. Paper-importer focuses on the final content-object generation step.

f19f8b6278c8.title: When to Use This Skill
f19f8b6278c8.content: . | User says “upload”, “scan”, “process document”, “intake” | User drops a file into library/ | User mentions WHO, L1, L2, guideline, normative | User wants to convert a raw document into content objects | Files appear in library/ that haven’t been processed yet | .

4e3fefb26f82.title: library/ Directory Convention
4e3fefb26f82.content: library/ <document-id>/ intake.json ← processing state + metadata original.pdf ← raw upload (PDF, scan, etc.) original.tex ← or LaTeX source extracted-text.md ← OCR or parser output (intermediate) extracted-blocks.json ← structured extraction (intermediate) mapping.json ← label/section mapping decisions README.md ← human notes about the document . intake.json schema . { "id": "who-anc-2016", "title": "WHO Recommendations on Antenatal Care", "source": { "type": "pdf", "url": "https://...", "fetchedAt": "2026-03-25T..." }, "format": "pdf|latex|scan|html|docx", "pipeline": { "stage": "uploaded|extracted|structured|mapped|generated", "extractedAt": null, "structuredAt": null, "generatedAt": null, "errors": [] }, "classification": { "type": "guideline|paper|report|standard", "domain": "health|physics|math|...", "normativeLevel": "L1|L2|L3|null" }, "chapters": [], "blockCount": 0, "targetPaper": "content/<paper-id>/" } .

7f99c987c29b.title: Pipeline Stages
7f99c987c29b.content: Stage 1: Upload (→ uploaded) . Place raw files in library/<document-id>/. Create intake.json with source metadata. Files are committed to git for reproducibility. Supported formats: . | PDF — academic papers, scanned guidelines, reports | LaTeX — .tex source bundles | HTML — web-published guidelines, standards | DOCX — Word documents (WHO often distributes as Word) | Images — scanned pages (PNG, JPG, TIFF) | . For academic papers, prefer the MCP fetch path (added 2026-05-22): when the session network allows the upstream host, use paper-search-mcp (arxiv / PubMed / bioRxiv / medRxiv) or openalex-paper-search (alex-mcp; OpenAlex catalog) rather than curl/WebFetch. The MCP tools return canonical metadata and the PDF in one call, eliminating the OCR-then-extract-then-name dance. See paper-importer.md §Phase 1 for the per-tool routing table. Sandboxed Claude-Code-on-the-web sessions (github-only allowlist) cannot reach those hosts; in those sessions, queue the fetch onto a normal-network machine per bib-qa.md §Batch intake pipeline. Stage 2: Extraction (→ extracted) . Convert raw format to extracted-text.md: . 🛑 THIS SECTION WAS 82 LINES BEHIND ITS SOURCE UNTIL 2026-09-16, and the stale version named tools instead of programs. It said “PDF (text) | pdftotext or PDF.js” and “PDF (scan) | Tesseract OCR / Claude vision” — which is precisely the aspirational text scripts/pdf-extract.py was written to replace. That script’s own docstring records the cost: “document-intake advertises ‘Handles OCR extraction’ and its routing table sends scanned PDFs to ‘Tesseract OCR / Claude vision’ — but nothing implemented that, so in practice an agent reached for a Python PDF library, got an empty string or an import crash, and had to guess what went wrong.” . The folio-assistant copy was fixed then; this one was not, and qou is where all 715 ingested documents live. The drift gate (gen-skill-docs.ts --check) covers the published docs site only — nothing checks this file against its source, so assume it can go stale again and diff it against skills/folio-paper-adapter/document-intake.md before trusting it. The scripts live in the folio-assistant clone, not in qou. Invoke them across the boundary, as scripts/migrate-uploads-to-library.py already does: . | Format | Extraction method | . | PDF (text) | folio-assistant/scripts/pdf-extract.py — a 5-rung ladder, not one tool | . | PDF (scan) | pdf-extract.py exits 2, then folio-assistant/scripts/pdf-ocr.py (Tesseract) or Claude vision | . | PDF (sections) | folio-assistant/scripts/pdf-structure.py → structure.json + sections/*.md | . | PDF (tables/figures) | folio-assistant/scripts/pdf-tables.py → tables.json, multipage stitching included | . | LaTeX | Direct parse (strip preamble) | . | HTML | Readability + turndown | . | DOCX | Pandoc → markdown | . | Images | Claude vision API | . python3 folio-assistant/scripts/pdf-extract.py FILE.pdf -o extracted-text.md python3 folio-assistant/scripts/pdf-ocr.py FILE.pdf --outdir library/<doc-id>/ # scans only python3 folio-assistant/scripts/pdf-structure.py FILE.pdf --outdir library --ocr python3 folio-assistant/scripts/extract-candidates.py library/<doc-id>/ . Four things that matter here and are not guessable from the table: . | The exit code is the diagnosis. pdf-extract.py returns 0 text · 2 no text layer, i.e. a scan · 3 a parser problem on a file that does have text · 4 bad usage. So “swap libraries” and “you need OCR” are decided by evidence rather than by trying things. | pdf-structure.py READS the OCR cache; it never runs OCR. On a scan the order is pdf-ocr.py first, pdf-structure.py --ocr second. The other way round the sections come out empty. | An OCR’d document whose structure was never re-run is invisible to a sections/ grep — which is corpus-grep path 5. This is the same “fourth tier” AGENTS.md describes — and the producer it could not name is pdf-ocr.py, whose output path is literally page-{i:03d}.txt. | The OCR and table backends are NOT in the shipped image. c767a0cc30ca.content: Detecting WHO guideline structure . WHO guidelines follow predictable patterns: . RECOMMENDATION N: <recommendation text in bold/box> Remarks: - Implementation note 1 - Implementation note 2 Summary of evidence: <narrative text> GRADE table: <quality assessment> . Label conventions for guidelines . | Element | Label pattern | Example | . | Recommendation | def:who-<guideline>-rec-<N> | def:who-anc-rec-1 | . | Evidence summary | prose:who-<guideline>-evidence-<N> | — | . | Remark | rem:who-<guideline>-remark-<N> | rem:who-anc-remark-1 | . | Good practice | prop:who-<guideline>-gps-<N> | prop:who-anc-gps-1 | . | Research priority | conj:who-<guideline>-research-<N> | conj:who-anc-research-1 | . Cross-referencing WHO recommendations . WHO recommendations often reference each other and external evidence. Map these to uses[] in content objects: . export default definition({ label: "def:who-anc-rec-3", title: "Recommendation 3: Daily iron supplementation", uses: ["def:who-anc-rec-1"], // references Rec 1 tags: ["imported", "source:who-anc-2016", "L1", "normative"], meta: { source: "library/who-anc-2016", strength: "strong", quality: "moderate", gradeLevel: "⊕⊕⊕◯", } }); .

f2f1aa073506.title: Evidence Appraisal
f2f1aa073506.content: Named by: Copy out materialized content — to work on somebody else’s bytes, Translation review and adjudication, Translation Workflow, Review task, Copy a knowledge-graph asset into a folio, KG to public portal, Remote-mount a dependency, Publish an ArchiMate model — every picture derived from it, Publish a web app — declared, translated, built at its own route, Contributor feedback on a working draft, Board: place a note . Appraise and grade a body of evidence against the grading system the folio declares. This skill supplies the procedure; it does not supply the system.

ab6b205cd1d5.title: Why this skill names no grading system
ab6b205cd1d5.content: Which grading system applies is a methodological commitment of the folio and the body that publishes it; the platform holds no subject matter, and a hardcoded system would leave every folio that uses another one working around the platform. An evidence-retrieval process in the content layer judges certainty “per the grading system the folio declares”. This skill covers what appraisal is, what it attaches to, and what has to survive as a record afterwards. Domain layers supply concrete grading systems as refinement skills and code lists (certainty levels, rating reasons, recommendation strength). Each applies only when declared, never as a default; with nothing declared, appraisal is refused.

69db44a6a528.title: Responsibilities
69db44a6a528.content: . | Appraise the body of evidence assembled for one question, not a citation | Record the grade with its reasons, not as a bare label | Distinguish “the evidence is weak” from “there is not enough to judge” | Re-appraise when the body changes, and say what moved the grade | Refuse to grade when no system is declared, rather than picking one | .

7e1ee13e6ac5.title: The unit is the body, not the citation
7e1ee13e6ac5.content: The grade attaches to the body of evidence for one PICO question. This is why appraisal sits after retrieval’s parallel join and not inside the fan-out: the three retrieval classes (trusted L1 sources, trusted L2/L3 content, data repositories) contribute to one judgement; grading each branch separately would produce three numbers that answer no question. A single citation does not carry a certainty grade.

f8b74a4dd532.title: “Cannot appraise” is a third state
f8b74a4dd532.content: Three outcomes; “not appraisable” is not a low grade: . | outcome | means | . | graded | the body was appraised and carries a certainty | . | not appraisable | too little retrieved, or no declared system, or the question was not framed as PICO | . | gap recorded | nothing authoritative was found, and that is the finding | . Never collapse “not appraisable” into the lowest grade: “we looked and the evidence is poor” is not “we could not look”. A recommendation resting on the first is weak; one resting on the second is unsupported.

326bcfd5d452.title: Inputs
326bcfd5d452.content: . | The framed PICO question — without it the search is not reproducible and the appraisal is not checkable | Candidates that passed an authority check, so authority is a resolved fact rather than an assertion in the citation | The grading system declared by the folio | .

d1337b56df41.title: Outputs
d1337b56df41.content: . | A certainty judgement for the body, in the declared system’s own vocabulary | The reasons, in enough detail that a later reader can tell whether they would still hold (decision-audit); a grade without them cannot be reviewed, only re-litigated | Any gap, recorded as a gap rather than as a low grade | .

59728974a904.title: This has nothing to do with formal content
59728974a904.content: A graded body of empirical evidence is never an input to a formal deductive proof. In a content type with a formal proof layer, a formal claim’s assertion is discharged by its machine-checked proof sibling and by nothing else; certainty grading belongs to empirical guidance about the world, where the question is what the evidence supports. An empirical grade in a formal proof obligation is a category error.

795281c70a4f.title: Actors
795281c70a4f.content: . | Author / guideline developer (lead) | Domain SME (domain judgement, supplied by the content-type layer) | Content Reviewer (checks the grade’s reasons survive, not the grade itself) | .

f2bcff97708e.title: Evidence review — the same rule, a second instance
f2bcff97708e.content: Skill evidence-review: Evidence review as an instance of untainted verification — the separation of the appraising party from the drafting party, what recurring surveillance in a living guideline shares with a stale QA verdict, and which of guideline methodology’s rules are fenced rather than shipped. Named by: Contributor feedback on a working draft . Skill id: evidence-review · Package: folio-core . untainted-verification states a generic discipline. Evidence review — the appraisal of the evidence behind a recommendation — is one instance of it; the translation round trip is another. Two unrelated instances are evidence that the discipline is generic, where one would only be an example.

420f0d080d1c.title: The rule
420f0d080d1c.content: The party that drafted the recommendation does not write the evidence appraisal for it. Guideline methodology already separates the systematic review team from the guideline development group for the same reason: a party assessing its own output is comparing a thing with its own paraphrase of itself. | untainted-verification | here | . | producer | whoever drafts the recommendation | . | checker — given the artefact, and nothing that would let it shortcut | the appraisal, given the question and the evidence, not the draft’s conclusion | . | adjudicator — given the intent and the checker’s output, never the artefact | the evidence-to-decision judgement | . An appraiser shown the drafted recommendation is told the answer before being asked the question; its “the evidence supports it” measures the instruction, not the literature.

299ff1413991.title: Recurring surveillance is staleness, generalised
299ff1413991.content: A living guideline is updated as evidence appears, so its appraisal is a verdict with an expiry. A QA verdict is hashed to its subject and stales when the subject is edited; a living-guideline verdict stales when the evidence base changes, even though the subject did not. The field_hash covers only inputs in the repository; an external corpus is not covered. Either way, “verified on DATE against THESE inputs” is a different claim from “verified”, because a reader given the second cannot tell a current verdict from a lapsed one. A folio implementing surveillance gives each verdict an explicit expiry, as bean-blocking (opt-in cat-harness.work-plan) does for a block: a verdict with no expiry cannot be told from an abandoned one.

e8d3a2d2b09b.title: The fencing analysis — which rules are the platform’s, and which are not
e8d3a2d2b09b.content: Run through domain-fencing (opt-in cat-harness.kg-ops)’s three questions, in order, first-to-answer wins: . | candidate rule | Q1 rationale survives translation? | Q2 domain in mechanism or vocabulary? | Q3 needs the domain installed? | verdict | . | appraiser ≠ drafter | yes, word for word | vocabulary | no | platform — it IS the spine | . | a verdict carries what it was verified against, and when | yes — it is the field_hash argument | vocabulary | no | platform | . | a finding is upheld by opening the cited source, never by trusting the rule’s wording | yes | vocabulary | no | platform — and already the practice in voice-who-guideline-development | . | certainty rated across the GRADE domains | no | mechanism | yes | fence | . | PICO question formulation | no | mechanism | yes | fence | . | evidence-to-decision framework tables | no | mechanism | yes | fence | . | a search strategy is re-runnable — databases, dates, query recorded | yes in rationale | mechanism is bibliographic | yes | fence the mechanism, keep the rationale (it is the row above) | . Three rows are platform rules; the four fenced rows are a folio’s methodology, not a backlog. Nothing is shipped for the fenced rows — empty criteria would let a consumer scan nothing and report a clean run. A folio that wants them declares them in its own repository.

fe106e5db0be.title: What this skill does NOT do
fe106e5db0be.content: It asserts no clinical or empirical claim, and the platform must not. The mechanism carries process — who may rule on what, given what. The evidence is the folio’s and the judgement is the guideline group’s; a platform that shipped a default answer to either would be asserting on their behalf.

342451ce7954.content: . | untainted-verification — the discipline. Read it first; this skill adds only what evidence review instantiates. | translation-manager §”The agentic round trip” — the other instance. | voice-who-guideline-development in the IRIS replica’s style guide — how a recommendation is worded: the language of normative statements, not the process that produces them, which is this skill. | domain-fencing — the three questions, and why a fenced rule is correctly located rather than missing. | .

e71546bd923a.title: External registry — the role’s contract
e71546bd923a.content: Skill external-registry-contract: The contract the external-registry role is held to: what a trusted registry outside this layer must provide for a portal to verify what it received, and what the verifier does when it cannot. The narrowest contract the diagrams require. A mechanical role’s skill is a contract to test against, not instructions to read. Named by: KG to public portal . external-registry in scenarios/roles.json is played by an external actor: trusted registries and observatories outside this layer’s control. A role played by something we do not run is still a role, and its skills are its contract: what we rely on it to do. A contract is not an instruction; it is what the diagrams assume.

42c2642f1e54.title: Where the diagrams lean on it
42c2642f1e54.content: One lane names this role: Lane_Portal in processes/kg/kg-to-portal.bpmn, holding P_Verify and GW_Verified. What that lane’s documentation, the task’s, and kg-to-portal §”Trust” require of the registry is the whole contract — nothing more is claimed.

c714c765e9c0.title: What it must do
c714c765e9c0.content: . | Publish the trust anchors a verifier resolves a signer’s key from — for GDHCN, a WHO SMART Trust DID trustlist (did.json), served as static JSON (PROD: tng-cdn.who.int/v2/trustlist/…). | Serve a slice by its hierarchical path, …/$domain/$participant/$usage/did.json, with - as a wildcard, so a verifier fetches only what it needs. | Nothing else. Whether a package signature can be expressed for GDHCN verifiers at all is an open question in kg-to-portal, not a promise of this role. | .

2cc37ed341fa.title: What the verifier does when the contract is not met
2cc37ed341fa.content: An unreachable registry is unknown, never a pass: GW_Verified routes it as it routes a mismatch, to the last good version (End_Rejected). This side of the contract is ours, and it is what makes relying on a party we do not control safe. Needs the owner’s review: this contract is inferred from one diagram. The test in tested-by: holds the side of it that is ours: one lane names this role, it holds P_Verify and GW_Verified, and GW_Verified serves the bytes only on a match, sending every other answer to End_Rejected. Lines 1 and 2 above are the registry’s own behaviour on a network this repository does not reach, and nothing here tests them.
