82df6697bee4.title: Skills it satisfies
82df6697bee4.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. translation-adjudication . A person’s word on a translation, carried from the translation review page or a block’s 🌐 pane to the record: anyone proposes text, which joins the ranked candidates; an owner, member or collaborator adjudicates, by accepting a catalogue or choosing one string’s translation with a reason; it is filed as a translation-adjudication/v1 issue; a workflow checks the author and the catalogue’s hash, writes the records, re-runs the auto-pick and opens a PR; a maintainer merges it. Use for “review the translations”, “this string is mistranslated”, “why was my review not recorded”, and when wiring a layer for review. Locale sign-off is a separate act, not this one. Source: cat-harness/library/skills/library-core/translation-adjudication.md. Also satisfied by: github, translation-adjudicate, translation-review-page, translation-status-viewer. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/translation-adjudication/{input,output}.schema.json).

ba1bfc298391.title: Build, check and (on request) publish a layer’s own site, or a branches/ preview
ba1bfc298391.content: From a checkout whose layers arrive by remote mount: mount the pinned closure, install, run the layer’s own gates (--pre), compose the harness chrome for THIS layer, run its source steps, build with Jekyll at the base path read from the git remote (/<repo>, or /<repo>/branches/<branch> for a preview), run the post-build steps (mount-instance-docs, pdf-viewer, set-html-lang, publish-id-lookup, rail-standalone-pages), and check that every relative or base-rooted link in every page resolves to a file under the site, reading each page with an HTML parser. Any failing step stops the run; a link that does not resolve means nothing is published. It never decides to publish: only --publish does, and then a root publish keeps branches/ and _render-log/ on the branch, and a preview replaces only its own branches/<branch>/. |   |   | . | Tool | build-instance-site | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/build-instance-site.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/build-instance-site/build-instance-site.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

ba7d858d7ff2.title: Convert a checkout to a root index.config.json
ba7d858d7ff2.content: Write the root index.config.json (folio-index-config/v1) that says which layers the checkout instantiates, where each comes from (source.local or source.remote) and which owns / (site.landing), from the root *.config.json files and the declaration’s remoteMounts. With --write it moves remoteMounts off the declaration into source.remote entries, writes the generated .gitignore block, and renames a legacy <name>.mount-lock.json to index.lock.json. Without a flag it prints the index it would write. Idempotent: a re-run merges what the declaration gained, and refuses an entry the index already holds differently. A root config naming no layer is reported as unmatched-config and not imported, because what to do with it is a person’s decision. |   |   | . | Tool | index-config-migrate | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/index-config-migrate.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/index-config-migrate/index-config-migrate.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

f018c2b3ade2.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. index-config . index.config.json at an instantiation root says which harnesses the checkout instantiates, where each one comes from (local, or a remote mount pinned to a SHA), each layer’s config INLINE in its entry (a legacy <name>.config.json is only imported until --inline retires it), and which harness / is. Covers instantiated against declared, landing resolution and its error case, index.lock.json and its legacy fallback, the reserved index stem, the generated .gitignore block and its gate, and index-config:migrate (with --inline) for separated repositories. Source: cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/index-config.md. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/index-config/{input,output}.schema.json). remote-mount . Bring a harness, and every layer it depends on, into a checkout that does not hold it, from another repository at a pinned commit, as declared directories with a lock: a source.remote entry in the downstream’s root index.config.json (legacy: remoteMounts on its declaration) and mountDefaults on the harness. Covers when to mount and when to subscribe instead, why there are no submodules and no .deps/, the transitive closure through needs and gitlinks, overrides by id, the lock, and the three states. Source: cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/remote-mount.md. Also satisfied by: build-instance-site, instantiate-harness, kg-retrieve-npm, mount-from-lock, npm, subgraph-index-package. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/remote-mount/{input,output}.schema.json).

b88350cf3dd7.title: Draw a document’s tables and figures from its ArchiMate data, and check the model against the document’s relationship rules
b88350cf3dd7.content: For each table a layer’s cat-archimate.config.json lists under tables, rewrites the block’s Markdown table from an archimate-relationship-rules/v1 file (relationship-rules: source, relationship, target, note; relationship-types: picture, verb, meaning), keeping the caption and footnotes. For each figure under figures that names an svg, writes the view as SVG (the same drawing as the view’s page). For a rules table that names a model, reports the rules the model never uses, the relationships no rule covers, the rules ArchiMate’s relationship table refuses, and the relationship types the rules use without a meaning. The rules are in charge: nothing is rewritten from the model. |   |   | . | Tool | archimate-blocks | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/archimate-blocks.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/archimate-blocks/archimate-blocks.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

00e992395b53.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. translation-adjudication . A person’s word on a translation, carried from the translation review page or a block’s 🌐 pane to the record: anyone proposes text, which joins the ranked candidates; an owner, member or collaborator adjudicates, by accepting a catalogue or choosing one string’s translation with a reason; it is filed as a translation-adjudication/v1 issue; a workflow checks the author and the catalogue’s hash, writes the records, re-runs the auto-pick and opens a PR; a maintainer merges it. Use for “review the translations”, “this string is mistranslated”, “why was my review not recorded”, and when wiring a layer for review. Locale sign-off is a separate act, not this one. c2a66543e5c1.title: Skills it satisfies
c2a66543e5c1.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. archimate-models . ArchiMate models as knowledge-graph content: how a layer declares the Archi models it holds, what the archimate subgraph gives every model, view, element and relationship (an IRI, a thin page, and every view drawn as SVG from the model’s own diagram, and its metamodel derived and checked), how to version the models, how to wire them into a folio’s staging build and navbar, how to count and lower the crossed lines in a view before committing it, why every view carries a plain-language key, why names are the source’s own terms linked to their SKOS concepts, and why no Java, no Archi CLI and no Archi HTML report is ever part of the pipeline. Read before adding, authoring, publishing or rendering an .archimate file, before citing an ArchiMate element from prose, and before reaching for Archi’s own tooling in CI. Source: cat-harness/skills/ui/ui-core/archimate-models.md. Also satisfied by: archimate-actors, archimate-blocks, archimate-crossings, archimate-detangle, archimate-metamodel, archimate-pages. 3176a5ca09eb.title: Check declared credential needs against workflow use and expiry, by name
3176a5ca09eb.content: Compare each repository’s declared credential needs (credentials/needs.json, profile and registry) with the secrets.NAME expressions its workflows reference (GitHub Actions’ dollar-and-double-brace form, said in words because this text is rendered on a Jekyll page), with the secret names GitHub lists when a token allows it, and with any recorded expiry. NAMES ONLY — no value is ever read. Findings: used-not-declared, declared-not-used, declared-not-present, present-not-declared (reported, never deleted), naming advisories, and expiry (≤30 days minor, ≤7 major, expired critical). Exits 2 when anything could not be determined, which outranks clean; else 1 on a major or critical finding; else 0. |   |   | . | Tool | secrets-check | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/secrets-check.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/secrets-check/secrets-check.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

7b3ec24fd549.title: Instantiate a harness over a repository that has none: pin, mount, open the setup-only PR, render the preview
7b3ec24fd549.content: The scripted step of the initiation process (getting-started.bpmn, the repo-conversion skill §4). Reads the harness’s declaration at its pin and every needs, transitively (a need beside the layer that needs it unless –repo-of says otherwise, at its default branch’s tip unless –pin says otherwise, its declaration’s name checked), seeds them all into the repository’s index.config.json with the consent given (remote-mount --seed --whole), sets site.landing to the harness, site.agentRun and mountApprovers, mounts the closure (remote-mount: index.lock.json and the .gitignore mounts block), installs it as root workspaces with the hoisted linker, writes the root bootstrap (.github/cat.ts and .github/mount-from-lock.sh from cat-harness-tools templates/root-bootstrap/) and sets the root’s cat script to bun .github/cat.ts, so bun run cat … mounts the layers itself on a later fresh clone, re-renders the agent surface from the mounted generators, runs the harness’s instantiate:<harness> checkout script when a mounted layer declares it, and commits on a branch (default harness/). Then, unless --local, pushes the branch, provisions gh-pages when absent (`pages-bootstrap --provision`), opens the setup-only PR, runs `prepare:` when declared (what the site is built from and nobody commits, such as an IG's AST) and renders the branch's preview at gh-pages branches// (`stage-local`); with --local the site is built and composed and nothing is pushed. It imports only node:*, so it runs from a fresh clone of cat-harness-tools before anything is mounted: it lays the platform's own closure, at the pins the repository will mount, into a temporary root to run the mount from. On a repository with nothing mounted yet, run the same file from a fresh clone: `git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/litlfred/cat-harness-tools /tmp/cht && bun run /tmp/cht/scripts/instantiate-harness.ts …`. Two more flags, not declared as ports because no constrained type carries them yet: `--pin =` pins one layer of the closure, `--repo-of =<owner/repo>` says where a need lives. |   |   | . | Tool | instantiate-harness | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/instantiate-harness.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/instantiate-harness/instantiate-harness.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

14a66ba369e1.title: Skills it satisfies
14a66ba369e1.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. repo-conversion . Lay folio-assistant over a repository that already exists, without losing or silently moving what is in it. Scans the tree read-only, classifies candidate files into library (external source) and content (authored here) with an explicit third bucket for what it cannot classify, scans outside the content tree for mathematical evidence and refutations, lists the content markers (an IG, a DAK, processes, work items, library, Lean, folio manifests) the harness could declare and declares only the ones the person picks, puts the three questions the scan cannot answer to the author as selections, and hands ingestion to one agent or a small swarm. Use when a user wants an existing repo converted to a folio, asks to import what is already there, asks whether their PDFs/notes/drafts can come along, or asks what else in a repository an existing harness could declare. Source: cat-harness/skills/conduct/conduct-core/repo-conversion.md. Also satisfied by: folio-init. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/repo-conversion/{input,output}.schema.json). remote-mount . Bring a harness, and every layer it depends on, into a checkout that does not hold it, from another repository at a pinned commit, as declared directories with a lock: a source.remote entry in the downstream’s root index.config.json (legacy: remoteMounts on its declaration) and mountDefaults on the harness. Covers when to mount and when to subscribe instead, why there are no submodules and no .deps/, the transitive closure through needs and gitlinks, overrides by id, the lock, and the three states. Source: cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/remote-mount.md. Also satisfied by: build-instance-site, index-config-migrate, kg-retrieve-npm, mount-from-lock, npm, subgraph-index-package. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/remote-mount/{input,output}.schema.json).

ArchiMate models as knowledge-graph content: how a layer declares the Archi models it holds, what the archimate subgraph gives every model, view, element and relationship (an IRI, a thin page, and every view drawn as SVG from the model’s own diagram, and its metamodel derived and checked), how to version the models, how to wire them into a folio’s staging build and navbar, how to count and lower the crossed lines in a view before committing it, why every view carries a plain-language key, why names are the source’s own terms linked to their SKOS concepts, and why no Java, no Archi CLI and no Archi HTML report is ever part of the pipeline. ac3e46bd9e2f.title: Run every existing security check as one named release step
ac3e46bd9e2f.content: Run the repository’s security checks — workflow injection, secret leaks, lockfile pinning, the toolchain pin, QA reviewer permission, materialised-asset fixity — plus two advisories (dependency advisories, third-party action SHA pinning), each by name as argv. Every check is reported as pass, fail or unknown; a blocking check that fails OR could not be run refuses the release, because could-not-check is never clean. Advisories are reported and never block. db3a08400cfb.title: Skills it satisfies
db3a08400cfb.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. kg-separation . Separate a Knowledge Graph into its own repository — as a CONTENT repository (files to read, no code) and a TOOLS repository (the code that writes and checks it) — once it is too large, or its consumers or cadence differ. The end-to-end method: the signals that trigger it, the preconditions, eleven stages each with the command that gates it, the owner’s decision points, how identifiers, QA and publication move, how the parent consumes the result, rollback, and the post-move sweep that a move between the pair owes before the parent re-pins. graph-detanglement owns stages 1–3; this skill owns the rest. Bootstrap + bootstrap-tools and cat-harness + the tools layer are the worked examples. Source: cat-harness/skills/kg/graph-management/kg-separation.md. Also satisfied by: mount-from-lock, package-exports, rewrite-moved-paths, separation-cutover-check. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/kg-separation/{input,output}.schema.json). kg-affordances . The four affordances of a conformant knowledge graph — browse, materialise, instantiate and copy-into-folio — which capabilities each requires, how each writing verb degrades cleanly when no write capability is available, and how copying an asset stamps KgAsset.source provenance. Source: cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/kg-affordances.md. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/kg-affordances/{input,output}.schema.json).

98549f157ed5.title: Rewrite paths that still name a moved file’s old layer — never in a record
98549f157ed5.content: After a move between two layers lands, find every mention <from>/<prefix>/<rest> in the scanned tree’s tracked files and rewrite it to <to>/<prefix>/<rest> only when the file exists under the destination root and not under the source root. Records are never read: beans, todos, memory, proposals, wireframes, QA results, upstream pins, vocab mappings, provenance figures and terminologies, and test fixtures (DEFAULT_RECORD_GLOBS; the CLI’s --keep <glob> adds more, generated trees among them, which their generators rewrite — a glob is not a shell-safe argument type, so it is not a declared input). Reports by default with file and line; --write applies; --check exits 1 while a rewrite is owed. |   |   | . | Tool | rewrite-moved-paths | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/rewrite-moved-paths.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/rewrite-moved-paths/rewrite-moved-paths.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

The node below is the definition this page was drawn from, and is embedded in the page as application/ld+json. { "@context": "https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.context.jsonld", "@id": "https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/rewrite-moved-paths.jsonld", "@type": "https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool", "partOf": "https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld", "name": "rewrite-moved-paths", "title": "Rewrite paths that still name a moved file's old layer — never in a record", "description": "After a move between two layers lands, find every mention `<from>/<prefix>/<rest>` in the scanned tree's tracked files and rewrite it to `<to>/<prefix>/<rest>` only when the file exists under the destination root and not under the source root. Records are never read: beans, todos, memory, proposals, wireframes, QA results, upstream pins, vocab mappings, provenance figures and terminologies, and test fixtures (`DEFAULT_RECORD_GLOBS`; the CLI's `--keep <glob>` adds more, generated trees among them, which their generators rewrite — a glob is not a shell-safe argument type, so it is not a declared input). Reports by default with file and line; `--write` applies; `--check` exits 1 while a rewrite is owed.", "install": { "none": true }, "invoke": { "shell": "bun run cat paths:rewrite-moved" }, "io": { "inputs": [ { "name": "fromName", "schema": "https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tool-types.schema.json#/$defs/Slug", "description": "The moved files' old layer, as paths spell it (e.g. the harness).", "required": true, "arg": { "flag": "--from-name" } }, { "name": "fromRoot", "schema": "https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tool-types.schema.json#/$defs/RepoPath", "description": "That layer's root on disk.", "required": true, "arg": { "flag": "--from-root" } }, { "name": "toName", "schema": "https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tool-types.schema.json#/$defs/Slug", "description": "The layer the files moved to.", "required": true, "arg": { "flag": "--to-name" } }, { "name": "toRoot", "schema": "https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tool-types.schema.json#/$defs/RepoPath", "description": "That layer's root on disk.", "required": true, "arg": { "flag": "--to-root" } }, { "name": "prefix", "schema": "https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tool-types.schema.json#/$defs/RepoPath", "description": "A moved directory, repeatable (e.g. `scripts`, `pipeline`).", "required": true, "arg": { "flag": "--prefix" } }, { "name": "scan", "schema": "https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tool-types.schema.json#/$defs/RepoPath", "description": "The git checkout whose tracked files are read; default the source root.", "required": false, "arg": { "flag": "--scan" } }, { "name": "write", "schema": "https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tool-types.schema.json#/$defs/Flag", "description": "Apply the rewrites.", "required": false, "arg": { "flag": "--write" } }, { "name": "check", "schema": "https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tool-types.schema.json#/$defs/Flag", "description": "Exit 1 while any rewrite is owed; write nothing.", "required": false, "arg": { "flag": "--check" } } ], "outputs": [ { "name": "rewrites", "schema": "https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tool-types.schema.json#/$defs/Count", "description": "Rewrites made or owed, each with file and line; mentions left alone; record files not read." } ] }, "satisfies": [ "kg-separation" ], "requirements": { "runtime": [ "bun", "git" ], "network": false } } .

da46939b4843.title: Skills it satisfies
da46939b4843.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. sub-kg-lifecycle . A sub-KG is a knowledge graph staged as a directory inside a harnessed repository, declared as its own layer, that may later leave for a repository of its own. The lifecycle: declare it in place, grow it, stage it for separation (one import seam, the separation guard, a self-contained rehearsal), and then, each behind an explicit owner confirmation, create the repository, copy the staged contents in with history, re-point the declaration, verify on a fresh clone and delete the in-repo copy. The light sibling of kg-separation: use this for a DATA layer that leaves whole, and kg-separation when a graph must split into a content repository and a tools repository. Source: cat-harness/skills/kg/graph-management/sub-kg-lifecycle.md. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/sub-kg-lifecycle/{input,output}.schema.json).

986e2ac3016a.title: Apply a vocabulary mapping table
986e2ac3016a.content: Carry one source record into a target vocabulary by a declared folio-vocab-mapping/v1 table: each source field becomes the predicate its row names, in the table’s order, with a DERIVED target (such as dcterms:title rendering skos:prefLabel) copied from its authoritative one so the two cannot drift. A table is shaped like a FHIR ConceptMap: an existing ConceptMap, R4 or R5, is representable as one without loss (fromConceptMap), and a table can be produced as a ConceptMap (toConceptMap), which returns every loss rather than dropping anything silently. a23de4ef6237.title: Every reference a journey or a workshop names resolves
a23de4ef6237.content: Read every user-scenario and workshop node in the checkout through the layers’ declared directories, with the journeys viewer’s own resolver, and resolve what each names: actors (personas, a step’s lead, experiences[].actor, handoff.from/to, illustrationStyle.cast[].actor), user stories, realisedBy BPMN files (instance-relative) and the element ids in them, uses blocks in a directory declaring building-blocks, req: requirements, FHIR examples and a step’s dak assets (data sets, decision tables, indicators) in a fhir-artifact-index (could not determine while the index is built at publish), illustration.src files, follows/partOf/parts/includes journeys (parts and includes forming no cycle; an includes held against the call activity its step’s realisedBy names, could not determine when the call names no process), the trustLadder code list and each record.state code of it, and ArchiMate views; and each workshop’s scenarios, steps[] {scenario, step} and <scenario>#<step> refs; each device screen’s owner and personCard actors, its steps[] {scenario, step}, and the FHIR examples its qr and recordList blocks name; and every persona’s avatar image path. Every journey is a DAK user scenario (the kind specialises it): its DAK personas, the roles its persona actors play, must be non-empty and each a declared role; a persona may be an actor or (0.4.0) a role. What is derived is not also written: a listed part’s follows or partOf, personas equal to the parts’, a lead equal to the lanes’ first actor, are each a redundant finding, and a 0.4.0 step with no experiences whose lanes no persona plays is a finding. A node that does not parse is a finding. One line per finding, naming the layer, file and step. 876cc1f80970.title: Skills it satisfies
876cc1f80970.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. asset-extraction . Reading a container — a zip, a PDF, a saved web page — into the knowledge graph. What goes in by default (metadata), what does not (contents), the three timestamps that sit near each other and mean different things, and why a producer string is evidence. 822175a990a8.title: Check that an ArchiMate model’s fhir-actor tags point at the IG’s FHIR ActorDefinitions
822175a990a8.content: Actors come first: the IG’s ActorDefinitions are written from the DAK’s personas, and an ArchiMate model only points at them. For one model a layer’s cat-archimate.config.json names, this reads every element carrying the Archi property fhir-actor, whose value is an ActorDefinition’s canonical URL, and the IG’s ActorDefinitions: FSH InstanceOf: ActorDefinition under input/fsh/, and FHIR JSON under fsh-generated/resources/ or input/resources/, each canonical being <sushi-config canonical>/ActorDefinition/<id> unless its url says otherwise. It fails on a value that is not a canonical URL, a tag that names no ActorDefinition, an element kind that cannot be an actor (a data object, a goal), and a type mismatch (a #person actor on an application or technology element, a #system actor on a business actor or role). It warns about each ActorDefinition no element realizes; --strict makes that a failure. --json prints element → actors and actor → elements, for page back-links. It never writes an ActorDefinition or any FSH, and never matches boxes to actors by name. |   |   | . | Tool | archimate-actors | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/archimate-actors.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/archimate-actors/archimate-actors.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

dc9c665adcd4.title: Skills it satisfies
dc9c665adcd4.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. archimate-models . ArchiMate models as knowledge-graph content: how a layer declares the Archi models it holds, what the archimate subgraph gives every model, view, element and relationship (an IRI, a thin page, and every view drawn as SVG from the model’s own diagram, and its metamodel derived and checked), how to version the models, how to wire them into a folio’s staging build and navbar, how to count and lower the crossed lines in a view before committing it, why every view carries a plain-language key, why names are the source’s own terms linked to their SKOS concepts, and why no Java, no Archi CLI and no Archi HTML report is ever part of the pipeline. Read before adding, authoring, publishing or rendering an .archimate file, before citing an ArchiMate element from prose, and before reaching for Archi’s own tooling in CI. Source: cat-harness/skills/ui/ui-core/archimate-models.md. Also satisfied by: archimate-blocks, archimate-check, archimate-crossings, archimate-detangle, archimate-metamodel, archimate-pages. Bootstrap + bootstrap-tools and cat-harness + the tools layer are the worked examples. Source: cat-harness/skills/kg/graph-management/kg-separation.md. 9a12a4464567.title: Screen a hand-over for injected instructions, field by field
9a12a4464567.content: Before a model reads a sub-agent’s report, a delegated prompt, a tool result or a comment from someone who is not the principal, screen it against a declared schema whose top-level fields are control (steers what the receiver does) or data (content it reads). A finding in a control field, or any field the strict schema does not declare, is REFUSED, so a report cannot extend the delegator’s plan. A finding in a data field is QUARANTINED: the original is kept and marked, never stripped. The patterns are a deterministic tripwire (instruction overrides, role and turn spoofs, fence breaks, tool-call syntax, hidden Unicode, exfiltration links, pipe-to-shell), a mitigation and not a guarantee. Exit 0 clean, 1 refused, 3 quarantined, 2 could not determine. |   |   | . | Tool | handover-screen | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/handover-screen.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/handover-screen/handover-screen.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

eafb552bb90d.title: Publish a folio’s or an IG’s site from the agent’s own checkout — the one agent publish path
eafb552bb90d.content: Build a repository’s site in the agent’s checkout and push it to the publish branch, as a preview or as the main site, without an Actions runner. Which build is read from the repository: a declared site.build recipe (built by build-instance-site), else the reusable workflow its own workflow files call — folio-staging.yml for a folio, the WHO SMART Base IG’s ghbuild.yml for a FHIR IG, whose build job is planned step by step and run as written. For an IG it then applies the harness chrome over the built output (sync-docs-harness, then rail-standalone-pages --foreign-site --instance <the IG>): every page gains the rail and the icon row #fa-navbar-row, and the IG’s own content is left byte for byte. A root publish is REFUSED when the chrome cannot be applied, and a clean root deploy is refused over any root whose index.html wears the icon row unless the new output does too, so a chromed root is never replaced by bare IG Publisher pages. Every run prints its plan first, and the plan lists the chrome step; --plan stops there, --dry-run composes the commit in a temporary worktree and pushes nothing, --artifact writes a claude.ai Artifact bundle instead. |   |   | . | Tool | stage-local | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/stage-local.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/stage-local/stage-local.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

e3af20d1aac8.title: Package one pin’s subgraph index files for a hydrated mount
e3af20d1aac8.content: Pack every built index.jsonld and index.hydrated.jsonld under a layer’s <docs>/subgraph/<harness>/ into ONE npm package for one pin — <harness>-subgraph-index@0.0.0-pin.<sha>, with a folio-subgraph-index/v1 manifest giving each file’s sha256 — through pack-tarball (bun pm pack), which also writes the tarball’s folio-binary-release/v1 record. It builds nothing: run subgraph:jsonld first. 4680bd7284d0.title: Replay a committed mount lock with nothing but Node
4680bd7284d0.content: Lay down every remote mount index.lock.json records — each layer fetched at the lock’s full SHA (sparse, blob-filtered), each directory verified against its treeDigest, a mismatch undone and reported — importing only node:*, so it runs on a fresh clone before any layer is present. It never decides what to mount: remote-mount writes the lock (and checks trust); this only replays it. Refuses to write over a path with tracked files or bytes that no longer hash to the lock. f6e1c1f1a3ed.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. remote-mount . Bring a harness, and every layer it depends on, into a checkout that does not hold it, from another repository at a pinned commit, as declared directories with a lock: a source.remote entry in the downstream’s root index.config.json (legacy: remoteMounts on its declaration) and mountDefaults on the harness. Covers when to mount and when to subscribe instead, why there are no submodules and no .deps/, the transitive closure through needs and gitlinks, overrides by id, the lock, and the three states. Source: cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/remote-mount.md. Also satisfied by: build-instance-site, index-config-migrate, instantiate-harness, kg-retrieve-npm, npm, subgraph-index-package. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/remote-mount/{input,output}.schema.json). kg-separation . Separate a Knowledge Graph into its own repository — as a CONTENT repository (files to read, no code) and a TOOLS repository (the code that writes and checks it) — once it is too large, or its consumers or cadence differ. The end-to-end method: the signals that trigger it, the preconditions, eleven stages each with the command that gates it, the owner’s decision points, how identifiers, QA and publication move, how the parent consumes the result, rollback, and the post-move sweep that a move between the pair owes before the parent re-pins. graph-detanglement owns stages 1–3; this skill owns the rest. Bootstrap + bootstrap-tools and cat-harness + the tools layer are the worked examples. Source: cat-harness/skills/kg/graph-management/kg-separation.md. Also satisfied by: declaration-resolution, package-exports, rewrite-moved-paths, separation-cutover-check. 1c8d81685430.title: Publish a built site to gh-pages as a full replace
1c8d81685430.content: Lay a built _site onto a gh-pages checkout as a FULL REPLACE and push it, keeping the open pull requests’ staging previews: each attempt re-reads the branch, re-runs restore-staging and keep-shared-payloads against what is on it now, replaces the tree, commits docs(gh-pages): site from <sha> and pushes. A rejected push is rebuilt, never rebased (a rebase would re-apply the replace over a preview a sibling just deployed), up to three attempts. A restore that cannot read the branch stops the publish. A site that matches the branch is a no-op, not a failure. It publishes and does not verify: the workflow’s verify step runs after it. |   |   | . | Tool | publish-gh-pages | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/publish-gh-pages.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/publish-gh-pages/publish-gh-pages.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

69118d965687.title: Journeys viewer
69118d965687.content: Draw every journey (user-scenario) and workshop (workshop) in the checkout as static pages at the route of the visualiser a layer declares for this Tool, <locale>/<instance>/<id>/: an index of all journeys, grouped by layer (each a sub-graph page), each parent’s parts nested under it in its order with optional and repeating parts marked (an older file’s partOf children after them, ordered along follows), and a plain DAK user scenario with no steps listed as one; one page per journey, its parts in order and the journeys it is a part of, a journey map with a lane and a feeling curve per persona, then each step, linked to the journey it includes, with its BPMN drawing (the step’s flow nodes highlighted), user stories, requirements, FHIR examples, building blocks, the DAK assets it uses (data sets, decision tables and indicators, linked into the IG) and ArchiMate views; and the workshop layer, the questions for the room on each step, a page per workshop and per module, job aids, and printable A3/A4 sheets; and each device screen (device-screen) that shows a step a workshop presents, drawn as a static device mock (phone, tablet, scanner, desktop, kiosk) with its owner beside it, in the workshop’s Device Demo, linked both ways with the walkthrough. A persona’s picture (meta.persona.avatar) is drawn wherever the persona appears. Layers below the declaring one are read through their declarations, so a downstream site shows the journeys of the layers it mounts too. |   |   | . | Tool | journeys-viewer | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/journeys-viewer.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/journeys-viewer/journeys-viewer.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

92c1224d3e14.content: Each port names a shared type by IRI, so two Tools for one skill can be checked for interchangeability. |   | port | type | required | description | constraint | . | in | markdown | Flag |   | Emit the block the session-start sweep prints. ALWAYS exits 0: the sweep runs it as if ! …; then, and a non-zero exit would print the report AND declare it unchecked every time CI is red. | boolean · A boolean switch — projects to a bare flag, with no value word | . | in | warn | Flag |   | Report only, never fail. For a caller that wants the state without a verdict. | boolean · A boolean switch — projects to a bare flag, with no value word | . | in | out | RepoPath |   | Write the markdown report to a file AND keep the exit code — which --markdown cannot do, since it always exits 0. Its own flag, so one API call is not spent twice. | string · pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9._][A-Za-z0-9._/-]*$ · A path relative to the repository root. No .. segments. | . | out | report | Markdown |   | One row per workflow. Five verdicts, not two: green, red, running, superseded (a red whose workflow file changed after the failing run, so the verdict is against code that no longer exists), and possibly-stale (a red that has not re-run in a week). Three exit codes carry them to a caller that reads no rows: 0 nothing is red, 1 something is, 2 COULD NOT LOOK — the API was unreachable, or --out could not be written. A caller must never read 2 as either verdict. --markdown and --warn always exit 0 by design, so a caller wanting the verdict uses neither. | string · Markdown text. Not admissible as a command-line argument — see INJECTION_SAFE. | .

89f90361ea62.title: Skills it satisfies
89f90361ea62.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. translation-manager . Translation lifecycle management for folio content. Covers gettext PO/POT extraction and injection, TranslationNode manifests as KG nodes, official vs unofficial translations, staleness tracking, sign-off workflow, automatic badge rendering, the poSources fallback resolution chain, and translating into several locales as a team: one extraction, a PR per locale to main, FHIR terms as CodeSystem supplements, the untainted round trip as run, and the per-locale QA report. Source: cat-harness/library/skills/library-core/translation-manager.md. Also satisfied by: translation-inject, translation-platforms, translation-roundtrip-record, translation-signoff, translation-status, translation-validate. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/translation-manager/{input,output}.schema.json).

63973b1c9b1c.content: Searches for a less tangled drawing of each view: a line may be re-routed straight or orthogonally (an L, or a Z through a free lane between boxes), and two same-size boxes in the same parent and row or column may swap places. A change is kept only if it lowers crossings + lines through boxes + lines drawn on top of each other. 6c3899169b53.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. translation-adjudication . A person’s word on a translation, carried from the translation review page or a block’s 🌐 pane to the record: anyone proposes text, which joins the ranked candidates; an owner, member or collaborator adjudicates, by accepting a catalogue or choosing one string’s translation with a reason; it is filed as a translation-adjudication/v1 issue; a workflow checks the author and the catalogue’s hash, writes the records, re-runs the auto-pick and opens a PR; a maintainer merges it. 68a191531357.title: Collect candidate translations from open engines
68a191531357.content: Ask one or more open, self-hosted machine translators — OPUS-MT (Helsinki-NLP Marian models, CC-BY 4.0, run locally) and/or a self-hosted LibreTranslate (AGPL, Argos models) — for CANDIDATE translations of each empty or fuzzy string, so no freemium API quota is involved. Candidates are appended to <locale>/<catalogue>.candidates.json (translation-candidates/v1) for a reviewer to choose among on the translation review page; a candidate whose placeholders or markup do not round-trip is not recorded. Candidates are never a barrier to having a translation: an EMPTY msgstr gets the first good candidate, marked #, fuzzy; a non-empty msgstr is never overwritten. The translation node records the source (generatedBy: "machine", model, time); official is never set, and a candidate is never a verdict. A catalogue that says DO NOT MACHINE-FILL, or whose node is official, gets candidates but no fill. |   |   | . | Tool | translation-candidates | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/translation-candidates.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/translation-candidates/translation-candidates.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

6b964f2a59bc.title: Skills it satisfies
6b964f2a59bc.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. translation-refresh . The translation watcher: a scheduled fresh session that keeps every locale of every layer current after the source moves. Cold start, then, per layer, detect, refresh the templates, merge them into each locale, translate only the new and fuzzy strings with the fixed terms, run the gates, round-trip the changed strings, write the QA report, open one PR to main, merge it only where the layer declares merge-when-green, and report source mistakes as one issue. Use for “refresh the translations”, “a template check failed”, and when scheduling or running the watcher. Source: cat-harness/library/skills/library-core/translation-refresh.md. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/translation-refresh/{input,output}.schema.json). translation-candidate-source . The one interface every candidate-translation engine meets: for a layer’s catalogues, append candidate translations per string to the translation-candidates/v1 sidecar, each carrying its source, and seed an empty msgstr with the first candidate marked fuzzy. An agent model and the open machine-translation engines (OPUS-MT, LibreTranslate / Argos) are interchangeable behind it. Use when adding an engine, choosing one, or producing candidates for review. Source: cat-harness/library/skills/library-core/translation-candidate-source.md. Also satisfied by: translation-candidates-agent, translation-platforms. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/translation-candidate-source/{input,output}.schema.json).

067507b03a95.title: Skills it satisfies
067507b03a95.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. translation-adjudication . A person’s word on a translation, carried from the translation review page or a block’s 🌐 pane to the record: anyone proposes text, which joins the ranked candidates; an owner, member or collaborator adjudicates, by accepting a catalogue or choosing one string’s translation with a reason; it is filed as a translation-adjudication/v1 issue; a workflow checks the author and the catalogue’s hash, writes the records, re-runs the auto-pick and opens a PR; a maintainer merges it. Use for “review the translations”, “this string is mistranslated”, “why was my review not recorded”, and when wiring a layer for review. Locale sign-off is a separate act, not this one. Source: cat-harness/library/skills/library-core/translation-adjudication.md. Also satisfied by: github, translation-adjudication-workflow, translation-review-page, translation-status-viewer. 7a58fe2cd915.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. archimate-models . ArchiMate models as knowledge-graph content: how a layer declares the Archi models it holds, what the archimate subgraph gives every model, view, element and relationship (an IRI, a thin page, and every view drawn as SVG from the model’s own diagram, and its metamodel derived and checked), how to version the models, how to wire them into a folio’s staging build and navbar, how to count and lower the crossed lines in a view before committing it, why every view carries a plain-language key, why names are the source’s own terms linked to their SKOS concepts, and why no Java, no Archi CLI and no Archi HTML report is ever part of the pipeline. Read before adding, authoring, publishing or rendering an .archimate file, before citing an ArchiMate element from prose, and before reaching for Archi’s own tooling in CI. 55fe598df765.content: Reached as:allgithub action (6)inProcess (23)manual (8)mcp (22)cli (128)152 of 152 shown | tool | what it does | invoked | satisfies | i/o | qa | . | agent-memory · JSON-LDAgent memory assembler | Assemble every declared memory directory’s nodes into each agent’s memory, per vendor: Claude Code’s .claude/agent-memory/<agent>/MEMORY.md (a marked region, injected when the subagent starts) and Antigravity’s workspace skill .agents/skills/<agent>-memory/SKILL.md. For one model a layer’s cat-archimate.config.json names, this reads every element carrying the Archi property fhir-actor, whose value is an ActorDefinition’s canonical URL, and the IG’s ActorDefinitions: FSH InstanceOf: ActorDefinition under input/fsh/, and FHIR JSON under fsh-generated/resources/ or input/resources/, each canonical being <sushi-config canonical>/ActorDefinition/<id> unless its url says otherwise. 2df5f878a0d9.title: Tools — cat-harness
2df5f878a0d9.content: The Tool nodes cat-harness declares in its tools graph — one instance’s slice of every instance’s tools. As an API: OpenAPI document · MCP tool list · API reference. A skill states a capability generically: what an actor needs to know to perform a task. A Tool is one concrete way to exercise it, with an installation, an invocation and typed inputs and outputs. One skill may be satisfied by several tools, and one tool may satisfy several skills. They are separate graphs and this is the tools one. The relation between them is satisfies, and it runs from a tool to a skill — this tool is one way to do that, never this skill is a tool. 152Tool nodes 58skills satisfied 128invoked as a shell command 22reachable over MCP

Track where you are inside a running process — which task, in which swimlane, under which role — and recover deliberately when you find yourself outside it. 5539357e541d.content: The Tool nodes cat-harness-tools declares in its tools graph — one instance’s slice of every instance’s tools. As an API: OpenAPI document · MCP tool list · API reference. A skill states a capability generically: what an actor needs to know to perform a task. A Tool is one concrete way to exercise it, with an installation, an invocation and typed inputs and outputs. One skill may be satisfied by several tools, and one tool may satisfy several skills. They are separate graphs and this is the tools one. The relation between them is satisfies, and it runs from a tool to a skill — this tool is one way to do that, never this skill is a tool. 1Tool nodes 1skills satisfied 0invoked as a shell command 1reachable over MCP

Cross-layer wiring auditor — watches for newly-landed formal/analytic improvements (proofs, propositions, lemmas, axiom→theorem upgrades, witness data) on the default branch AND on open PRs, and checks whether each one has been wired into the production compute chain. Complements compute-audit (which scans for performance/correctness antipatterns inside scripts). Runs in two modes: REACTIVE (watch new commits / PR events) and IDLE-SWEEP (walk all existing content blocks and audit wiring). c6c8b56b38e4.title: ArchiMate model from the glossary
c6c8b56b38e4.content: Make an ArchiMate model agree with the instance’s folio-glossary/v1 terms whose focus is an ArchiMate element: elements matched by their skosConcept property (never by name) take the term’s prefLabel and definition, a term with no element gets one on no view, and the relationships the terms list are added. 04b17924d393.content: For every figure a source publication declares, report whether the folio built from it has a block and how computable it is: missing, excluded (signed off), picture (a PNG crop), linked (a picture linked to a model view), computable (a diagram, a table or a figure rebuilt by ArchiMate, BPMN, DMN, Mermaid, a class diagram or a generator), or cited (a picture kept on purpose, signed off). b1030d35503e.title: Skills it satisfies
b1030d35503e.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. figure-rebuild . Turn a figure into a computable diagram: every figure of a source publication when a folio is built from its L1 entry, and any hand-drawn figure in a folio, an IG or a demonstrator that is redrawn from a source. Every declared figure gets a block, and each one is rebuilt in the form its type calls for: an ArchiMate view, BPMN, DMN, a FHIR logical model, or an SVG generated from data, always from one schema-backed source. The PDF crop stays beside the rebuild as the cited source, and the rebuild keeps the original’s layout. The figure-coverage check counts what is missing and what is still only a picture. Source: folio-assistant-core/skills/library/ingestion/figure-rebuild.md. Also satisfied by: as-drawn-svg, diig-phases-svg, smart-approach-svg. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/figure-rebuild/{input,output}.schema.json).

30456d2c6d95.title: Build the review sheet’s Apps Script and a document’s Config tab
30456d2c6d95.content: Builds Code.gs (--script), the one Google Apps Script every review sheet runs (from review-sheet.gs), and one document’s Config tab rows (--config), filled from the folio’s review/public-comment/sheet-sync.json, its review anchors and the draft’s pdf-line-map.json. The script keeps a public-comment review sheet’s links and joins current: each comment No. links to its comment page; Sections, Page and Line no(s) link to the page of the frozen review draft; Review Change Sets joins its comments, suggested revisions, feedback and dispositions, each No. n linking to its row; and on both tabs Agentic status lists each pull request of the change-set, linked, with its status and what it changed, from the Agent tab. It reads the document’s URLs, tab and column names and data from the sheet’s Config tab (visible, locked to the owner), which the agent writes from these rows. A person pastes the script (one file) into the sheet once (Extensions > Apps Script) and runs installTriggers; from then on the sheet rebuilds itself within about a minute of an edit, with no agent. With "mode": "drafting" in the config it builds the drafting sheet instead: one Contributor Feedback tab where each row is a change set (ids assigned by the script), Sections picked from the document’s table of contents and linked to it, and Issue and Agentic status from the Agent tab. |   |   | . | Tool | review-sheet-sync | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/folio-assistant-core/tools/review-sheet-sync.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/folio-assistant-core/folio-assistant-core.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | folio-assistant-core | . | source | folio-assistant-core/tools/review-sheet-sync/review-sheet-sync.ts | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

bd6ede2f253c.title: Rank candidate glossary terms in prose by C-value
bd6ede2f253c.content: The scoring step of the automatic-term-extraction method: count the word n-grams of one or more Markdown or text files (not across punctuation, front matter or code), and rank them by C-value as Frantzi & Ananiadou 1996 define it, so nested multi-word terms are not swamped by the longer phrases that contain them. Tested against the paper’s own worked example (Table 2). Every row is a candidate; it writes nothing and promotes nothing. |   |   | . | Tool | c-value-terms | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/folio-assistant-core/tools/c-value-terms.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/folio-assistant-core/folio-assistant-core.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | folio-assistant-core | . | source | folio-assistant-core/tools/c-value-terms/c-value-terms.ts | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

Turn a figure into a computable diagram: every figure of a source publication when a folio is built from its L1 entry, and any hand-drawn figure in a folio, an IG or a demonstrator that is redrawn from a source. 6c8adb10dc0c.title: Move a review comment’s status
6c8adb10dc0c.content: A review-process task moves one review-comment/1.0.0 todo’s status (address, send back, resolve, adjudicate, withdraw) through transition(), which refuses any move the named BPMN task may not make. The comment is written to the folio’s todos graph (its declared todo-feedback directory) and, with --commit, committed to the edit-set’s FEATURE branch. 79662773814e.title: Skills it satisfies
79662773814e.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. review-comments . Reviewer comments on a folio’s edit-set, from a tagged pull-request comment to a structured todo on the review page. Covers the tag a reviewer types, how the comments are ingested into review-comment/1.0.0 todos, where the published review-comments.json comes from and when it refreshes, how a comment follows a renamed block and survives a removed one, who may change a comment’s status, and how to change this process. Use when a reviewer asks how to comment on a block, when the review page shows no comments or a wrong one, when editing the ingestion, or when a folio’s staging workflow is set up. Source: folio-assistant-core/skills/content/content-lifecycle-ext/review-comments.md. Also satisfied by: folio-review-comments, folio-review-coverage. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/review-comments/{input,output}.schema.json).

2928454aad31.title: Skills it satisfies
2928454aad31.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. figure-rebuild . Turn a figure into a computable diagram: every figure of a source publication when a folio is built from its L1 entry, and any hand-drawn figure in a folio, an IG or a demonstrator that is redrawn from a source. Every declared figure gets a block, and each one is rebuilt in the form its type calls for: an ArchiMate view, BPMN, DMN, a FHIR logical model, or an SVG generated from data, always from one schema-backed source. The PDF crop stays beside the rebuild as the cited source, and the rebuild keeps the original’s layout. The figure-coverage check counts what is missing and what is still only a picture. Source: folio-assistant-core/skills/library/ingestion/figure-rebuild.md. Also satisfied by: as-drawn-svg, figure-coverage, smart-approach-svg. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/figure-rebuild/{input,output}.schema.json).

e9f344459d8f.title: Skills it satisfies
e9f344459d8f.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. dublin-core-renderings . Render a catalogue’s Dublin Core records in the two standard forms an outside reader can use: Dublin Core XML, which a harvester reads, and JSON-LD bound to DCMI Metadata Terms. Each rendering is published beside the item’s page. Covers which records get one, which XML form is used and why, how every field maps from the record’s own data (never composed), what cannot be expressed and how that is reported, and the gate. Read this before changing the mapping, adding a catalogue layer, or linking a rendering from a page. Source: folio-assistant-core/skills/library/catalogue/dublin-core-renderings.md. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/dublin-core-renderings/{input,output}.schema.json).

5073ffe41c22.title: Skills it satisfies
5073ffe41c22.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. review-comments . Reviewer comments on a folio’s edit-set, from a tagged pull-request comment to a structured todo on the review page. Covers the tag a reviewer types, how the comments are ingested into review-comment/1.0.0 todos, where the published review-comments.json comes from and when it refreshes, how a comment follows a renamed block and survives a removed one, who may change a comment’s status, and how to change this process. 21ad8fcfc106.title: Check a review log and its repository’s issues for changes
21ad8fcfc106.content: The mechanical check a review-log watcher runs on every poll. Given a drafting sheet’s Contributor Feedback values and the folio repository, it reads the repository’s open and closed issues (leaving out pull requests, issues labelled no-sheet and, with --author, issues someone else opened) and compares a digest of them and of the cells people set (Title, Selected Sections, Contributor Feedback, Disposition, Ready for agent, Ready for merge, Dispositions confirmed; on a public-comment log also Committee Feedback, TWG (CS), TWG (human) and Change Set (human)) with the last check’s. Unchanged: it prints {"status":"unchanged"} and exits 0. Changed: it exits 10 and lists what changed (issue opened, updated or closed; a cell’s old and new text), the Contributor Feedback rows to append, one per issue that no row’s Issue cell links yet (Title the issue’s title, the first Contributor Feedback column @login (#N): first paragraph, Issue the issue’s URL; a closed issue’s row marked closed), and closedRows, the rows linking a closed issue, which the watcher hides with their text struck through. A read with no Issue column (a public-comment log’s Review Change Sets) tracks only issues labelled change-set unless --label says otherwise, and appends no rows: each open issue is reported as an issue-unlinked change instead. It writes no sheet and no issue: the watcher appends the rows and does the agent pass. With --accept it stores the new state for the next poll to compare against. |   |   | . | Tool | review-log-watch | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/folio-assistant-core/tools/review-log-watch.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/folio-assistant-core/folio-assistant-core.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | folio-assistant-core | . | source | folio-assistant-core/tools/review-log-watch/review-log-watch.ts | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

895df29e6cd8.content: Stage three of skill-pipeline-subject-indexing for MeSH: look up every candidate heading of a draft (a preferred heading, an entry term, or a descriptor id, with an optional qualifier) in NLM’s MeSH authority at id.nlm.nih.gov, current year. b96a54378f5b.title: Tools — folio-assistant-core
b96a54378f5b.content: The Tool nodes folio-assistant-core declares in its tools graph — one instance’s slice of every instance’s tools. As an API: OpenAPI document · MCP tool list · API reference. A skill states a capability generically: what an actor needs to know to perform a task. A Tool is one concrete way to exercise it, with an installation, an invocation and typed inputs and outputs. One skill may be satisfied by several tools, and one tool may satisfy several skills. They are separate graphs and this is the tools one. The relation between them is satisfies, and it runs from a tool to a skill — this tool is one way to do that, never this skill is a tool. 30Tool nodes 21skills satisfied 30invoked as a shell command 0reachable over MCP

c0a9a532ae6c.title: Tools
c0a9a532ae6c.content: As an API: OpenAPI document · MCP tool list · API reference. A skill states a capability generically: what an actor needs to know to perform a task. A Tool is one concrete way to exercise it, with an installation, an invocation and typed inputs and outputs. One skill may be satisfied by several tools, and one tool may satisfy several skills. They are separate graphs and this is the tools one. The relation between them is satisfies, and it runs from a tool to a skill — this tool is one way to do that, never this skill is a tool. 454Tool nodes 100skills satisfied 425invoked as a shell command 27reachable over MCP

c9d352312fb3.doc: Ingestion subprocess — build the L1 knowledge graph
c9d352312fb3.title: Steps
c9d352312fb3.content: Every one of the 7 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | Write dublin-core.jsonld (the record of truth)Task_Dublin | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | One standalone Dublin Core record per folder. dcterms is already this corpus’s JSON-LD vocabulary, so this extends a live context rather than introducing one. | . | Write manifest.jsonld referencing itTask_Manifest | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | Write manifest.jsonld for the folder: its @id, @type folio:SourceDocument, what it contains and its provenance, referencing the standalone dublin-core.jsonld as the record of truth rather than copying its fields. | . | Record assets[] — local path or remote URLTask_Assets | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | kind / role / url-or-path / checksum / retrieved. A SIBLING of library:, never inside it: LibraryRef is regenerated from the tree, so an authored URL placed there is dropped on the next sync. | . | Bind the folder to its bibliography slugTask_Bind | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | Bind the folder name to the document’s bibliography slug, so library/<bib-slug>/ and its citation key are the same string: a citation resolves to a directory without a lookup table between them. | . | Read glossary into candidate termsTask_Glossary | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | glossary-terms | The source’s glossary and abbreviations sections become candidate terms of a folio-glossary/v1 scheme with the Tool glossary-from-source, verbatim, each with source file#line, and an acronym as the notation of the term it expands. Terms a person owns are never changed, and only a person moves a term to authored. A source with no such section skips this step with nothing written. | . | Extract reference listsTask_References | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | l1-document-ingestion | Each reference list of the source (a References, Bibliography or Further reading section, in any of the six UN languages) becomes folio-reference/v1 nodes with the Tool references-extract: one node per cited work, provenance extracted, derivedFrom the section it was read from, and printed the entry exactly as the source prints it. Only fields read without guessing are set (address, DOI, ISBN, year, access date); a cited IRIS item the library holds gets heldAt. The nodes are the document’s own bibliography on the bibliography page. A source with no reference list skips this step with nothing written. | . | Link L1 nodes into the corpus graphTask_Link | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | Anything in library/ is L1 source content. A knowledge-graph reference from any artefact – paper, L2, L3 – resolves to it through library/. | .

3c749f2c2990.doc: Ingestion subprocess — derive content from the assets
3c749f2c2990.title: Steps
3c749f2c2990.content: Every one of the 8 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | Archive → greppable contents manifestTask_Archive | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | NOT IMPLEMENTED; see docs/document-ingestion.md. Tar/zip is opaque to every grep in the corpus until its contents are listed as data. | . | File info, sizes, hashes, timestamps, mimetypeTask_TechMeta | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | NOT IMPLEMENTED; see docs/document-ingestion.md. Mechanical and cheap; the checksum is what makes a remote asset verifiable. | . | Narrative description per image, localizedTask_Image | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | Applies equally to an image EXTRACTED FROM A PDF (Task_FiguresTables), not only to an uploaded one. An agent opens every image and vector render and records a verdict in the library’s image-verdicts.json: role (figure, logo or decorative), the reason, and a draft description in English plus ar, zh, es, fr and ru, which the apply-image-verdicts.ts arm lays over images.json on every ingest. Images judged figure are kept as WebP, quality 80, at most 1600 px; logos, decorative fragments and page scans are not. Every description stays a draft until a person confirms it with bun run cat narratives. Method: skill document-intake, “Figures and captioned tables: describe, keep, transcribe”. | . | Transcribe and translate audioTask_Audio | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | No Tool yet; the method, and the choice of recogniser, is skill audio-transcription. | . | Sheet names, headers, shape, narrativeTask_Tabular | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | Tools tabular-csv and tabular-xlsx, as CSVW (skill tabular-metadata). CSV and spreadsheet: tabs, column and row headers, sizes, and what the dataset is about. | . | Extract figures and tablesTask_FiguresTables | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | The pdf-images.py, pdf-vector-labels.py and pdf-vector-figures.py arms extract the raster images and the figures drawn as vectors (grouped and rendered). For every table the document’s structure declares, an agent reads the rendered page, checks cell text against the text layer, and writes tables/<label>.csv plus tables.csvw.json (folio-tabular-csvw/v1), with a draft description in the six UN languages; pdf-tables.py’s grid is a cross-check, not the answer. Owner, 2026-11-11 (who-iris): “actually extract the figures” and “any tables too”. Method: skill document-intake, “Figures and captioned tables: describe, keep, transcribe”. | . | Footnotes and the marks that call themTask_Footnotes | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | l1-document-ingestion | The pdf-footnotes.py arm (owner, 2026-11-11, “also foot notes/marks”): from the page layout, each note at the foot of a page and every superscript mark in the text that calls it, written to footnotes.json (folio-document-footnotes/v1) with the block that holds the page. The section text is not changed. Only a called note is a footnote; uncalled foot-of-page lines and marks with no note are listed, never dropped. OCR’d pages have no fonts and are reported unread. Method: skill l1-document-ingestion, “Footnotes and their marks”. | . | Cite the author of every narrativeTask_Provenance | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | A generated description is a claim by someone. Record whether a human or an agent wrote it, and for an agent the model version. An uncited narrative is indistinguishable from a transcription of the source. | .

78e4c076dc79.title: Steps
78e4c076dc79.content: Every one of the 6 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | Extract the text layerTask_ExtractText | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | The document has a text layer: extract it with pdf-extract (pdfminer.six, then a zero-dependency content-stream reader). Exit 2 means no text layer — a scan — and routes to OCR; it is not an empty document. | . | Check each page; OCR pages that failTask_PageCheck | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | l1-document-ingestion | Owner, 2026-11-11 (who-iris, card Q-ODD-1 = A): “force OCR when a page’s text layer fails a quality check”. A text layer can hold plenty of letters and still not be the page’s text: accents mapped to Greek letters (“dΘclaration”), Persian set in the wrong Arabic code points, words split by kerning (“au g m ente”), fake-bold words printed twice, mojibake. cat-harness-tools scripts/_text_quality.py checks every page against the document’s languages (dc.language.iso, or –lang-hint); the router then OCRs the document and pdf-structure.py –ocr takes the OCR text for the failing pages only, listing them in structure.json source.ocr_pages with the reason. When most pages of a document with no outline fail, the whole document is read from OCR, as for a scan. Method: skill l1-document-ingestion, “A text layer that is not text”. | . | OCR to ocr/page-*.txtTask_Ocr | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | Each page is read in the document’s languages (–lang-hint, from dc.language.iso), narrowed to the script the page shows. A page Tesseract is unsure of (mean word confidence under 70) is read again with each other installed script added, and the most confident read is kept: a French article’s Arabic abstract, or the Latin URLs in an Arabic document’s references. A document ingested this way keeps its text in ocr/ and only a stub in sections/, which the documented sections/ grep cannot see. That asymmetry is why the corpus-grep checklist has a fourth tier. The run also records WHICH SOFTWARE made the pages, in ocr/run-context.json: a folio-run-context/v1 (cat-harness schemas/run-context.ts, the record test runs and QA reports use for the same question), naming the OCR engine, the rasteriser and each language model with its version and the sha256 of the bytes that ran. Two OCRs of one scan can read differently (“Manual” and “Manval”), and without it neither could be told from the other or reproduced. | . | Split into sections/*.md with doc_brief front-matterTask_Sections | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | Contextual retrieval: a chunk in isolation loses what makes it mean anything, so each section carries the document brief. An outline is set aside when its entries are machine bookmark names (_GoBack, _Hlk…, “Blank Page”, a merged file’s name) or when under half of them name a heading the pages print, and the contents are inferred instead (diagnostics.outline_rejected). A section that would hold more than half of a document of 20 pages or more (and over 8,000 words), or over 20,000 words anywhere, is cut at the headings inferred inside it, else one section per page (diagnostics.oversized_split). Owner, 2026-11-11: “split single blocks that hold a whole book”. Method: skill l1-document-ingestion, “An outline that is not contents, and a section too long to be a block”. | . | Write structure.jsonTask_Structure | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | Write structure.json (pdf-structure/v1): doc id, TOC from the PDF outline or inferred from headings, page ranges, metadata, and source{} with the sha256 and a mimetype sniffed from the bytes, never the extension. A structure that could not be determined says so in structure_note rather than being rendered as one. For OCR’d text, source.runContext cites the OCR step’s run context by sha256. A title already known for the document (the catalogue’s dc.title, or one given with –title) is passed through as the raw title, so the sections’ doc_title does not carry a scan’s misreading. | . | Extract claim candidatesTask_Candidates | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | candidates.json holds extracted theorems and definitions. Proposals only – never adjudicated verdicts. | .

776232c16443.doc: Ingestion subprocess — the L1 completeness gate
776232c16443.title: Steps
776232c16443.content: Every one of the 4 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | Is every derived artefact present?Task_CheckDerived | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | L1 source to L1 KG is NOT complete while a required derived artefact is missing. This is the gate that makes the derivation steps obligatory rather than aspirational. | . | Round-trip translation QATask_RoundTrip | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | translation-manageruntainted-verification | Back-translate each localized narrative into its source language and compare the meaning, to catch semantic drift and bad terminology that a forward-only check cannot see. Agentic. Two parties are kept apart under untainted-verification: a back-translator that sees ONLY the target-language text, and an adjudicator that sees the original and the back-translation and rules. The verdict is recorded per block, under criterion translation-semantic-roundtrip in the block’s <block>.<locale>.translation-qa.json sidecar, by the translation-roundtrip-record Tool (translation-manager §5). A terminology miss is a different criterion, translation-terms-preserved (acronyms, numbers, URLs that must survive), so Gateway_Drift can tell the two apart. Never close this step by reversing the PO’s msgid→msgstr map: that returns the source exactly and scores 1.0 always. An empty translation-semantic-roundtrip entry list means “not yet run”, which is never a pass. | . | Adjudicate the flagged passageTask_FlagDrift | Reviewer (SME or editor) | calls Adjudicationdocument-intakeadjudication | A machine can detect that two readings differ. Which one is right is a human call. | . | Record the L1 completeness verdictTask_Verdict | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | Record the completeness verdict in three states — met, unmet, or not yet derivable — as bun run cat check:l1-complete reports it. Not-yet-derivable is never a pass. An unmet verdict opens a bean and returns to derivation; only a met one lets the entry into library/. | .

7d98ee34b144.doc: Ingestion subprocess — the L1 completeness gate
7d98ee34b144.title: Decisions
7d98ee34b144.content: Every one of the 2 decision(s) is documented. | decision | what decides it | branches | . | Drift or bad terminology?Gateway_Drift | Answered by the round-trip translation QA: did it flag semantic drift or a terminology miss? drift sends the passage to a person to adjudicate, since which reading is right is a human call; clean records the verdict directly. | drift → Adjudicate the flagged passageclean → Record the L1 completeness verdict | . | Which reading was right?GW_DriftOutcome | All three converge on Task_Verdict, and that is deliberate rather than the codes being decoration: this lane adjudicates ONE passage while Lane_0 still owns the completeness verdict as a whole, so the outcome of a passage is a REASON recorded against that verdict, never a different next step. The same shape criterion-adjudication uses, where three outcomes converge on one write because what makes an outcome legitimate is that its reason was recorded.What differs is what gets written and what it obliges. real is drift to fix in the translation. spurious is a false positive, and recording it is what stops the same passage being re-flagged every run. source-wrong points at the SOURCE rather than the translation — the one answer that sends work out of this process entirely, because no amount of re-translating a wrong source produces a right target. | the drift is real → Record the L1 completeness verdictfalse positive → Record the L1 completeness verdictthe SOURCE is wrong → Record the L1 completeness verdict | .
