fb276af755ed.title: Translation refresh — the watcher
fb276af755ed.content: Skill translation-refresh: The translation watcher: a scheduled fresh session that keeps every locale of every layer current after the source moves. Cold start, then, per layer, detect, refresh the templates, merge them into each locale, translate only the new and fuzzy strings with the fixed terms, run the gates, round-trip the changed strings, write the QA report, open one PR to main, merge it only where the layer declares merge-when-green, and report source mistakes as one issue. Use for “refresh the translations”, “a template check failed”, and when scheduling or running the watcher. Named by: Multi-locale translation, Translation refresh (watcher), Publish a web app — declared, translated, built at its own route . The watcher is the last step of a multi-locale translation, and it runs for as long as the translations exist. It is a scheduled fresh session in the translation-source-lead lane of translation-refresh.bpmn, which multi-locale-translation.bpmn schedules. This page is what that session follows, cold, with nothing remembered from the session that scheduled it. translation-manager is the reference for every term used here; read its §”Translating into several locales as a team” first. Generic on purpose. Nothing here names a layer. Where a step depends on the layer (where its pages live, which extractor writes its page templates, how its terminology supplements are built), the layer’s own AGENTS.md names it, and you read it there.

de5f9af78368.title: What wakes it
de5f9af78368.content: . | The schedule set when the watcher was armed. A run that finds nothing to refresh ends at once, and that is the usual run. | A template check that failed, on main or on a PR: a source change that did not refresh its templates. Run the watcher for that layer before anything else touches its catalogues. | .

420bb50be2a9.title: Cold start, once per run
420bb50be2a9.content: . | Clone each layer the run covers, and follow its AGENTS.md cold start to lay down every pinned layer from its index.lock.json. In a composed checkout that is, in order: clone the mounts the lock lists, bun install --frozen-lockfile, bun run cat mount:lock, bun run cat mount:remote:check. Never mount a layer at a floating ref, and never edit a mounted layer: a fix to one is a PR to its repository. | Attach each repository the run may push to. In a hosted session that is the session’s add-repository tool, with push access. A repository the run cannot push to is reported, and the run goes on with the others. | Note the merge policy. Each layer’s AGENTS.md (§ Translations) declares it. The default, when nothing is declared, is open only: the run opens PRs and merges nothing. A layer may declare merge-when-green (step 9). | .

3ae6544eb4d1.title: Per layer, in order
3ae6544eb4d1.content: <root> is the layer’s directory in the checkout. Every command below takes --instance <root>, so one checkout serves every layer. | step | command | moves on when | . | 1. detect | translation:status --instance <root>, translation:drift:check --instance <root>, translation:obsolete:check --instance <root>, and the layer’s template checks | any shows something to do | . | 2. refresh templates | the layer’s extractors (translate-bpmn --instance <root> --extract for diagrams; pages and glossary as its AGENTS.md names) | the template checks pass | . | 3. merge into each locale | msgmerge --update --backup=none, or translation:obsolete --instance <root> | every catalogue matches its template | . | 4. translate new and fuzzy | optionally candidates first: translation:candidates --instance <root> --engine opus-mt (Tool translation-candidates), then by hand or by agent, with the locale term base | no empty entry is left, and every fuzzy entry is either re-translated or a candidate awaiting review | . | 5. gates | below | every gate passes | . | 6. round trip | translation-round-trip.bpmn on the changed strings | both drift and not-drift are recorded | . | 7. QA report | translation:page-qa --instance <root>, and the report | it is written | . | 8. one PR | one per layer, based on main and targeting main | it is open | . | 9. merge | only under merge-when-green, all green, round trip no fail | merged, or left open and reported | . | 10. source mistakes | one issue on the source | filed, or none found | . | 11. prune rulings | the layer’s prune command, after the removal is on main | dry run clean, or a pure drop-and-renumber pushed | . 1. Detect . bun run cat translation:status --instance <root> # new, fuzzy, empty, per locale bun run cat translation:drift:check --instance <root> # each .po against the .pot beside it bun run cat translation:obsolete:check --instance <root> # msgids the source no longer yields . Then the layer’s template checks: translate-bpmn:check for its diagrams, and the page and glossary template checks its AGENTS.md names. Any of them failing, or any count above zero, is a change to refresh. Exit 2 is not “nothing to do”. These commands exit 2 when they cannot determine the answer, for example when a layer declares no translation-sources directory. Report it for that layer and go on to the next; never read it as current. 2. Refresh the templates . Re-run the layer’s extractors, once, for every locale. Diagrams: . bun run cat translate-bpmn --instance <root> --extract . Pages and glossary schemes: the extractors the layer’s AGENTS.md names. A generator that writes below a mounted layer leaves that mount modified; re-lay it from the lock afterwards, as the cold start says. 3. Merge into each locale . Merge each refreshed template into every locale’s catalogue: . | new strings arrive empty: they are the work of step 4; | changed strings arrive fuzzy, with the old translation kept as a hint; | obsolete strings are kept as #~ entries, never deleted, so the translation can be revived if the source comes back. | . A string that leaves the catalogue costs no round trip. Rulings are paired with strings by the hash of the msgid they judged, not by position (translation-manager §”The untainted round trip, as run”), so removing or reordering strings invalidates none of them. The removed strings’ rulings are dropped by step 11, after merge. With gettext installed, msgmerge --update --backup=none <locale.po> <template.pot> does all three. Without it, bun run cat translation:obsolete --instance <root> marks the obsolete entries, and the layer’s AGENTS.md names how its new strings are added. Then re-run step 1’s translation:drift:check: it fails while any catalogue still differs from its template. 4. Translate only the new and fuzzy strings . Translate the empty and fuzzy entries in every locale, and nothing else. A string already translated is not re-translated, even where you would have worded it differently today. Translate with the locale term base (translation-manager §”The locale term base”): a term a lower layer fixes keeps its fixed form. Clear #, fuzzy only on an entry you have actually re-translated. Machine candidates are allowed, and stay drafts. bun run cat translation:candidates --instance <root> --engine opus-mt (add ,libretranslate --url <self-hosted> for a second source) asks open engines for candidates for the empty and fuzzy entries, never a hosted freemium API. The candidates go to <catalogue>.candidates.json for the review page. An EMPTY entry also gets the first good candidate, #, fuzzy, so it is never left untranslated. A candidate whose placeholders do not round-trip is not recorded. The tool does not change a fuzzy entry that already has text, a plural entry, a catalogue that says DO NOT MACHINE-FILL, or a catalogue whose node is official (those get candidates only). Its strings stay fuzzy until you re-translate them or a person picks or accepts one on the review page. Do not clear the flag because a machine wrote the string. FHIR terms go into the locale’s one CodeSystem supplement, never into the resource. Translation-node manifests stay official: false, with generatedBy: "agent", or "machine" where the candidates step filled an empty entry. Write no status.json. A mistake in the source is not fixed here. Translate what the source says, and note the location for step 10. 5. Gates . bun run cat check:translation-officiality bun run cat translation:catalogue:check bun run cat translated-links:check bun run cat kg:locale:check --instance <root> bun run cat translation:glossary:check --instance <root> --locale <locale> . The first three read the checkout they run in and take no --instance, so run them from the checkout that holds the layer. Then the layer’s supplement build: the locale’s CodeSystem supplements compile with no SUSHI error and pass their structural checks (the command is in the layer’s AGENTS.md). Placeholders, tags and URLs are preserved: translation:page-qa reports a lost one as translation-terms-preserved. A gate that fails is fixed in the .po, the manifest or the supplement, and step 5 runs again. A glossary hit on a platform term in text of another subject area is a sense check, not a violation: read it, note it in the report, and change nothing because of it. 6. Round trip on the changed strings . Run translation-round-trip.bpmn on the strings this run translated, and only those. The method is in translation-manager §”The untainted round trip, as run”. When two separate parties cannot be dispatched, record “could not dispatch” with the reason: it is never a pass, and the PR says so. 7. QA report . bun run cat translation:page-qa --instance <root> . writes the per-catalogue sidecars under the layer’s test/results/translation-qa/. Beside them, write the locale’s report: the strings refreshed, each gate’s result, the round-trip counts (sampled, flagged, drift, not drift) with every drift ruling and its fix, the glossary violations and sense checks, and the source mistakes found. 8. One PR per layer, to main . One branch from main, one PR to main, carrying every locale this run refreshed for that layer. Never push to a source PR’s branch, and never to a branch that has already merged. The PR body links the QA report. 9. Merge, by the layer’s policy . The policy is the layer’s to declare, in its AGENTS.md: . | open only (the default): open the PR, merge nothing, report it. | merge-when-green: merge the run’s own refresh PR only when every check is green and the untainted round trip on the changed strings records no fail. Anything red, uncertain or failing is left open and reported to the owner; the next run looks again. | . Either way the translations stay unofficial: merging is not sign-off. Never merge a PR the run did not open, and never one to a repository the owner has said only a person merges. 10. Source mistakes: one issue . Every source-text mistake the translators noted goes into one issue on the source repository, with the location and the reading the translation took. Not one per locale, and not a fix in the translation: a fix to the source is a source PR, and the next run carries it to every locale. 11. Prune the rulings of removed strings, after merge . Only where the layer keeps per-string round-trip rulings on an attestations state branch; its AGENTS.md names the command, by convention translation-qa:prune. Run it once the PR that removed strings is on main, whoever merged it: . bun run cat translation-qa:prune # dry run against origin/main: each dropped ruling, each renumbered span bun run cat translation-qa:prune --write # apply it to the mounted attestations bun run cat state:push # push that one commit to the state branch . Push only when the dry run shows nothing but dropped and renumbered rulings. It drops a ruling only when main once held its string and no longer does, so a ruling recorded ahead of an unmerged PR stays; it never changes or adds a verdict. Never run it from the removing branch before that branch merges: the state branch serves main as well, and main would be left with strings that have no ruling. Nothing to prune is the usual result.

88592cc7144e.title: Never
88592cc7144e.content: . | Never re-extract per locale. Templates are refreshed once, for every locale. | Never re-translate a finished string, and never delete an obsolete one. | Never re-run the round trip because strings were removed or reordered. Rulings are keyed by content; step 11 tidies them mechanically. | Never write official: true. A person makes a translation official (human-translation-workflow). | Never read exit 2 as clean. “Could not tell” is reported, every time. | .

d10145b06584.content: The skill translation-refresh as its source file cat-harness/library/skills/library-core/translation-refresh.md writes it, rendered by gen-processes-viz.ts because it has no instruction page on this site — do not edit here. All processes .

235931834d22.title: Translation refresh (watcher)
235931834d22.content: Process_TranslationRefresh · advisory · 11 step(s) . Keep every locale current after the source moves: detect, refresh the templates, merge them into each locale, translate only what is new or fuzzy, check it, and land one PR per layer on main. You are in this process when the watcher scheduled by multi-locale-translation wakes, or when a template check has failed. It is the loop that process ends with. A fresh session can run it cold: the skill translation-refresh gives each step as a command, and each layer’s own AGENTS.md names what is particular to it. One run walks every layer in turn, and each layer with something to refresh gets its own PR. A refresh never re-translates a finished string. Obsolete strings are kept as #~ entries, new ones arrive empty, and only new and fuzzy strings are translated, with the terms the term base already fixes. The round trip runs on the changed strings only. Round-trip rulings are keyed by content: each is pinned by the hash of the msgid it judged (and of the msgstr), never by its position in the catalogue. So removing or reordering strings invalidates no ruling and needs no agent re-run. Once main no longer holds a removed string, its ruling is dropped mechanically by the prune step. i i i i i i i i i i i Actors: Locale translator · Source-language lead (watcher) .

19c4788601d2.title: Translation review and adjudication
19c4788601d2.content: Process_TranslationReviewAdjudication · advisory · 14 step(s) . A person’s word on a translation, carried from the page they read it on to the record. Candidate translations come from any engine and from anyone; a reader opens the review page or a block’s 🌐 pane, accepts what is there, or picks a ranked candidate or writes their own; that travels as a GitHub issue; a workflow checks it and opens a pull request; a maintainer merges it. You are in this process when a catalogue has a translation nobody has adjudicated: a machine, flagged or stale cell on the review page, or a string a block’s 🌐 pane shows as proposed, agent, mt, missing or stale. translation-workflow produces the machine translation and human-translation-workflow makes a locale official; this process sits between them and does neither. What it records is that ONE catalogue was read by ONE person who could be held to it, against the exact bytes they saw. Two rules hold throughout. Candidates are never a barrier to having a translation: an empty msgstr gets the first candidate, marked fuzzy, so the page always has something to show. And a reader’s text is a proposal until a collaborator chooses it: anyone may propose, and every proposal is appended to the candidates sidecar beside the others; only an owner, member or collaborator adjudicates, by choosing one text as the translation with a reason. A string nobody has adjudicated shows the best-ranked candidate, fuzzy and unofficial, unless an official source’s English matches the msgid exactly. Locale sign-off (X-Folio-Official, the locale’s status.json) is a separate, deliberate act that this process never performs. GitHub is one Tool here, not the process: the issue is the carrier of the verdict and the pull request the carrier of the record. Another forge carrying the same translation-adjudication/v1 record would be another Tool satisfying the same skill. i i i i i i i i i i i i i i Actors: Automated pipeline · Reviewer (adjudicator) · Maintainer .

13db69223c9f.title: Steps
13db69223c9f.content: Every one of the 14 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | Produce candidate translations (any engine)Task_TRA_Candidates | Automated pipeline | translation-candidate-source | One or more candidate sources write alternatives per string to translations/<locale>/<catalogue>.candidates.json (translation-candidates/v1), each candidate carrying its source: an agent model, an open machine-translation model, a web service, or a person. The engines are interchangeable behind one skill, translation-candidate-source: whichever runs, the same sidecar comes out. Writers append; a candidate is never a verdict. | . | Write the first candidate as a fuzzy msgstrTask_TRA_SeedFuzzy | Automated pipeline | translation-candidate-source | Candidates are never a barrier to having a translation. The first candidate becomes the msgstr, marked #, fuzzy: the page shows it, the status page counts it as needing review, and it stays the default until a person adjudicates the catalogue. | . | Build the review pageTask_TRA_ReviewPage | Automated pipeline | translation-adjudication | translation:status writes review.html beside the status page. Every site build, wherever the checkout has translations, publishes assets/translation-status/review.json (folio-translation-review/v1: every catalogue × locale, its state, and the hash of the catalogue’s bytes) and, per catalogue, its strings projection (folio-translation-strings/v1: every string in every locale, its status, its candidates ranked, and the default pick) — publish-translation-review.ts, run by the site build. The catalogue hash is what an adjudication is pinned to; the strings projection is what a block’s 🌐 pane draws. | . | Read the catalogue on the review pageTask_TRA_Review | Reviewer (adjudicator) | translation-adjudication | The reviewer opens the review page and reads one catalogue’s strings against their source, with the candidates beside each. | . | Open a block’s 🌐 translation paneTask_TRA_BlockPane | Reviewer (adjudicator) | translation-adjudication | On every page, source-language pages included, a block’s 📣 panel has a 🌐 pane that lists every locale’s current translation of the block, its status, and how it came to be (chosen.how, chosen.by). On a translated page its own locale comes first and the others are collapsed. ✎ Fix translation opens, per locale, each of the block’s strings with its candidates ranked as the auto-pick ranks them: the text; the source’s kind, id and version; who proposed it, linked to the issue it came from; the date; its QA results; a stale mark when it was made for another source text; whether an official source’s English matched exactly; and which one is the default. | . | Pick a candidate or write your ownTask_TRA_Choose | Reviewer (adjudicator) | translation-adjudication | For each wrong string: pick a ranked candidate, which fills an editable box (its source is recorded with the suggestion while its text is unedited), or type your own. Anyone’s text is a proposal. An owner, member or collaborator may also tick Choose as the translation and say why: the suggestion then carries choose: true and the reason, and it is recorded as the string’s translation only once the workflow has confirmed who they are. The suggestion carries the text the reviewer saw (current), so a choice against a catalogue that changed under them is caught. | . | File the adjudication issueTask_TRA_FileIssue | Reviewer (adjudicator) | translation-adjudication | Submit opens GitHub’s new-issue form prefilled with a readable summary and a translation-adjudication/v1 JSON block, labelled translation-adjudication and titled [translation review] …. The summary says, per string, whether the author proposes or chooses. When the record is too long for a URL the page copies the body for pasting instead. Filing it is the act of proposing, or, for a collaborator who chose, of adjudicating. | . | Plan the records (translation:adjudicate)Task_TRA_Plan | Automated pipeline | translation-adjudication | translation:adjudicate reads the issues event GitHub wrote, never the body from a shell variable: the body is untrusted and is only parsed as JSON. It decides every write before making any, and refuses rather than guesses. | . | Append every suggestion as a human candidateTask_TRA_Propose | Automated pipeline | translation-adjudication | Every suggestion, whoever filed it, is appended to the catalogue’s translation-candidates/v1 sidecar as {kind: "human", id: "github:<login>", by, issue}, with the msgidHash of the string it translates and its placeholder QA. A proposal is never refused for a changed catalogue and never conflicts with another: the sidecar keeps them all, ranked side by side. A record that does not parse, or that names another repository or another translations directory, is refused here. | . | Comment why nothing was recordedTask_TRA_Refuse | Automated pipeline | translation-adjudication | Every refusal, with its reason, as a comment on the issue (exit 3). No pull request is opened. A refusal is never a partial record dressed as a whole one; a new review is a new issue and a new instance of this process. | . | Write the choices and sign-offsTask_TRA_Write | Automated pipeline | translation-adjudication | A chosen suggestion becomes the string’s msgstr, not fuzzy, and its sidecar entry’s chosen records how: adjudicated, by whom, when, in which issue, why, and which candidate. acceptable: the catalogue’s translation node gets signedOffBy / signedOffAt, and each fuzzy string in it is adjudicated as it stands. Each adjudication appends an entry to the catalogue’s translation-qa attestation (criterion human-adjudication) naming the issue and the hash the person saw, and a proposal one under human-proposal; the attestation is append-only and checked against qa-attestations/v1 before it is written. The PO header X-Folio-Official and the locale’s status.json are never touched. | . | Auto-pick by rankTask_TRA_AutoPick | Automated pipeline | translation-adjudication | For each string nobody has adjudicated, its candidates are ranked: official 0, adjudicated 1, a person’s proposal 2, a translation platform (Weblate, Crowdin, Transifex) 3, an agent model 4, machine translation 5; a QA failure adds 10; ties go to the newest; a stale candidate, made for another source text, is never picked. An empty msgstr, or one that is itself an earlier auto-pick, takes the best: fuzzy and unofficial (chosen.how: auto), except an official candidate whose English matches the msgid exactly, which is written as auto-official. A collaborator’s choice, and text whose provenance is not an auto-pick, are never overwritten. translation-strings.ts applyAutoPick; the 🌐 pane ranks with the same function’s rules. | . | Open a ready PR and commentTask_TRA_OpenPR | Automated pipeline | translation-adjudication | Commit on translation-adjudication/issue-<n>, authored by the issue’s author, open a ready pull request that names the issue, and comment the summary on the issue: what was recorded and what was refused. | . | Review the PR; merge or closeTask_TRA_Merge | Maintainer | translation-adjudication | The maintainer checks that the PR writes down what the issue decided and nothing else, lets the layer’s checks run, and merges or closes it. | .

Yes seeds it. No leaves the .po alone: an existing translation is not replaced by a candidate, only offered beside it. | Yes → Write the first candidate as a fuzzy msgstrNo → Gateway_TRA_Seeded | . | Where does the reader start?Gateway_TRA_Entry | Two ways in, one record out. Review page: a reader working through a layer’s catalogues. A block's 🌐: a reader on any page who finds one block’s translation wrong, or wants to see it. Both file the same translation-adjudication/v1 issue. | Review page → Read the catalogue on the review pageA block’s 🌐 → Open a block’s 🌐 translation pane | . | Acceptable?Gateway_TRA_Verdict | Per catalogue, the reviewer’s verdict. Acceptable: the translation as it stands. Mistranslation: one or more strings are wrong, and the reviewer says what they should be. | Acceptable → File the adjudication issueMistranslation → Pick a candidate or write your own | . | Already recorded for this issue?Gateway_TRA_Once | The workflow runs for an issue that is labelled or titled as an adjudication, and once per issue: Yes when the issue’s branch already exists, and nothing more is done. | Yes → Already recordedNo → Plan the records (translation:adjudicate) | . | Event and declaration readable?Gateway_TRA_Determined | No when there is no event file, the event carries no issue with an author, or the layer has no declaration to resolve its translations directory from. That is “could not determine” (exit 2): the run fails, and it is never read as “nothing to record”. | No → Could not determine (the run fails)Yes → Append every suggestion as a human candidate | . | Author an owner, member or collaborator?Gateway_TRA_Author | Read from the event’s author_association, never from the body. Yes (OWNER, MEMBER or COLLABORATOR): the author’s acceptable verdicts and choose suggestions are adjudications. No: what they filed stays a proposal; an acceptable verdict or a choose from them is refused with a comment saying so, and their suggestions are still candidates for a collaborator to choose among. | No: proposals only → Auto-pick by rankYes → Any choice against an unchanged catalogue? | . | Any choice against an unchanged catalogue?Gateway_TRA_Hash | The pins bind adjudication only. Per verdict and per choice: is the catalogue’s hash today the one the page showed, does its path stay inside the translations directory, and is the suggestion’s current text still what the catalogue says? One that fails is refused with its reason (reload the page and choose again), and its proposal is kept. No when no choice or acceptance survives: the proposals still go on to the auto-pick. Yes when at least one survives, and the refusals are reported beside what was recorded. | No → Auto-pick by rankYes → Write the choices and sign-offs | . | Anything to record?Gateway_TRA_Anything | Yes when the issue added a candidate, a choice or a sign-off. No when every item in it was refused: nothing is written and no PR is opened. | No → Comment why nothing was recordedYes → Open a ready PR and comment | . | Merged?Gateway_TRA_Merged | No: the PR is closed and nothing is recorded; the issue stays as the account of what was asked. Yes: the records are in the repository. | No → Closed, not recordedYes → Verdict? | . | Verdict?Gateway_TRA_PerCatalogue | Decided once for each catalogue the merged PR records, by what it records: Accepted when the catalogue was found acceptable, Chosen when a collaborator chose a string’s translation, Proposed when only proposals went in. One issue can carry several catalogues, so one merge can end in more than one, a catalogue at a time. | Accepted → Catalogue reviewed (not official)Chosen → String adjudicated (not official)Proposed → Proposal recorded (fuzzy until chosen) | .

aa6bad5e8326.title: Translation round trip (untainted)
aa6bad5e8326.content: Process_TranslationRoundTrip · advisory · 6 step(s) . Did the meaning survive the translation? The untainted round trip on a sample of one locale’s strings, with the two parties kept apart: a back-translator who sees only the target text, and an adjudicator who sees only the source and the back-translation. You are in this process when multi-locale-translation or translation-refresh calls it, after the deterministic gates have passed. It is the translation instance of untainted-verification: the producer (the locale translator) draws the sample and never writes the verdict; the back-translator renders and rules on nothing; the adjudicator rules. GT_RoundTripQa in translation-workflow is the same check drawn as one step; this diagram draws its parties, because the separation between them is what makes the result a measurement. A first run samples every diagram label, the personas and scenarios, and a seeded random fraction of the rest; a refresh samples only the strings it changed. The third state is drawn: when two separate parties cannot be dispatched, the producer records “could not dispatch” with a reason, and that is never a pass. i i i i i i Actors: Locale translator · Back-translator · Round-trip adjudicator .

640338f6ef74.content: Every one of the 6 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | Draw the sampleTask_RT_Sample | Locale translator | translation-manager | On a first translation: every diagram label, every persona and scenario string, and a seeded random fraction of the rest, with the seed written down so the sample can be drawn again. 8ba4642997af.title: Translation Workflow
8ba4642997af.content: Process_Translation · advisory · 12 step(s) . The machine half of translation, end to end: extract the translatable strings, inject a catalogue back, check the result by back-translating it, and track whether the source has moved since. You are in this process whenever translation happens without a person having to be present. Two of its steps are the exception and are drawn in their own lane: a flagged passage is ADJUDICATED by a human, and a translation becomes official only when a human signs it off. human-translation-workflow is what happens when a person is doing the translating rather than checking it. Staleness is an END state that re-enters at the beginning, not a failure. A source change does not invalidate a translation’s accuracy; it invalidates its currency, which is a different fact and is why it is recorded rather than thrown away. i i i i i i i i i i i i Actors: Author (source content) · Agent / platform (automated) · Human reviewer / adjudicator .

4f1d5a2a2e59.title: Lanes — who acts
4f1d5a2a2e59.content: | lane | role | what it does here | . | Author (source content) | author | — | . | Agent / platform (automated) | authoring-agent | Everything in this process that runs without asking: extraction to a template, injection of a catalogue, the staleness comparison, and writing the official rendering once sign-off exists. It decides nothing a person would disagree about — every branch it takes is computed from a hash or a file’s presence.It is one lane rather than two because agentic and mechanical is a judgement rather than a line (see the role model), and nothing in THIS process turns on which of the two ran a step. Where that distinction does matter, the process says so by putting the step in the reviewer’s lane instead. | . | Human reviewer / adjudicator | translation-adjudicator | The only lane here that JUDGES. Mechanical translation QA produces candidates — a flagged passage, a terminology miss, a staleness verdict — and a candidate is not a finding until somebody decides it is. This lane is where that decision is made, and it is the lane that signs the translation off, because the actor who resolves a disputed passage is the one who can say the whole is fit to publish.Adjudicator rather than reviewer alone, and the distinction is the accountability: a reviewer reports, an adjudicator settles. The word is used here because the passage reaching this lane is one where a checker and a translator disagree, and somebody has to choose between them WITH a reason. That reason is the record, not the choice. | .

c67cf68a2457.title: Steps
c67cf68a2457.content: Every one of the 12 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | Extract translatable strings (POT)Task_PotExtract | Agent / platform (automated) | shared step GT_ExtractPottranslation-manager | Scan the source content and write the translatable strings to .pot files at the configured granularity: segment prose by paragraph, shield what must not be translated (math, code, labels, Lean companions) as placeholders, normalise whitespace, and extract metadata such as titles, alt text and captions. Tool: the translation_extract MCP tool. | . | Build and review the locale term baseTask_TermBase | Agent / platform (automated) | translation-manager | Before translating: build the locale term base from the layered glossaries, review it, and translate with it. Precedence, within one subject area (the scheme’s subject): the more authoritative (lower) layer fixes a term’s translation; a layer only adds. A match in another subject area is a sense check, not a violation. Each layer’s glossary is the directory it declares with the glossary graph typology. A fixed translation is an authored term with a non-empty, non-fuzzy msgstr in its scheme’s catalogue. | . | Produce translation (PO file)Task_Translate | Agent / platform (automated) | translation-manager | Translation of .pot → .po, with the locale term base, by one of:1. Existing PO from the WHO SMART Base IG (Weblate/Crowdin/Launchpad)2. Open machine translation as candidates: translation:candidates (Tool translation-candidates), OPUS-MT run locally and/or a self-hosted LibreTranslate, no freemium API. Each source’s text is a candidate in <catalogue>.candidates.json for the reviewer to choose among; a candidate whose placeholders do not round-trip is not recorded; an empty msgstr gets the first good candidate, tagged #, fuzzy; the node records generatedBy “machine”, never official. A catalogue marked DO NOT MACHINE-FILL gets candidates only.3. Agent (LLM) translation4. Human translatorResult: <locale>/block.po with msgid/msgstr pairs. A machine or agent string stays fuzzy and unofficial until a person picks or accepts it (translation review page) or signs it off (Task_Signoff). | . | Inject translations (PO → Markdown)Task_PoInject | Agent / platform (automated) | shared step GT_InjectPotranslation-manager | Read the .po file and the source .md, substitute msgstr for msgid, unshield the placeholders, and write the translated .md to translations/<locale>/. Check structure (paragraph count, heading levels) and completeness (no empty msgstr), and lint (doubled punctuation, orphaned placeholders). df99079526f9.title: Untainted verification — the producer never writes the verdict
df99079526f9.content: Skill untainted-verification: The party that produced an artefact does not write the verdict on it. How a checker and an adjudicator are dispatched with controlled context, the three rules that make it a measurement rather than a ritual, and the third state that lets it gate at all. Named by: Translation review and adjudication, Translation round trip (untainted), Translation Workflow, Adjudication, Criterion adjudication, Wireframe design review, Contributor feedback on a working draft, Ingestion subprocess — the L1 completeness gate . Skill id: untainted-verification · Package: sdlc-core . A secret scan, a schema validation, a back-translation and a systematic literature search differ in what they read and in what counts as a finding. They do not differ in this: . The party that produced the artefact does not get to write the verdict on it, and the checking party is given a controlled context rather than the run of the repository. Everything below is that sentence made operational, for any domain, because taking the translation vocabulary out of it changes nothing structural; translation-manager.md §”The agentic round trip” is the translation instance.

bb342d83da8a.title: The parties
bb342d83da8a.content: | party | is given | produces | . | producer | the task | the artefact | . | checker | the artefact’s declared checker_sees, and nothing that would let it shortcut | an independent rendering or finding | . | adjudicator | adjudicator_sees and the checker’s output — never the artefact itself | pass / warn / fail, each drift named | .

1d5c91c92f80.title: Three rules, and the failure each one stops
1d5c91c92f80.content: 1. Neither party sees what would let it shortcut. A back-translator shown the English writes the English back and the check passes vacuously. An adjudicator shown the French can talk itself into any reading of the back-translation. Neither failure raises an error; both produce a green verdict that measured nothing, which is worse than a red one. 2. The checker uses no tools, and says so. The artefact is in the repository. A checker with filesystem access can find what it was not given, and the verdict then measures its search rather than the artefact. Ask for a TOOLS_USED line and record the answer — UntaintedParty.tools_used. Absent means nobody asked, which is not the same as “no”. 3. One party doing both halves is not this check. It compares a thing with its own paraphrase of itself.

0d6e2ad8f022.title: The context is declared, not composed
0d6e2ad8f022.content: UntaintedDispatch on the criterion (schemas/sdlc/block-qa.ts) declares checker_sees, checker_withheld, adjudicator_sees and drift. A caller names a subject and a criterion; it does not hand-assemble a brief. That is not ceremony — the party composing a brief by hand is the producer, and rule 1 then breaks silently, one call site at a time. A declaration is also checkable, and untaintedPartitionDefects checks it: . | defect | what it means | . | undeclared | no untainted block. Reported, never skipped: nobody said is not nothing to check | . | overlap | a role visible to both parties — one of them is grading its own input | . | unpartitioned | a companion in depends_on that is in neither visible set; usually a role added later. Nobody decided | . | phantom | a role named in the declaration that the criterion does not depend on — the declaration describes something else | . Totality is the point of checker_withheld. Without it a newly-added companion role defaults into the checker’s view, or out of it, and either way the separation moves without anybody choosing. With it, the partition simply stops being total, which has a name. drift must say both halves. Told only what to look for, an adjudicator returns a style review and everything fails. The translation round trip states it well: synonyms, articles and re-ordering are not drift; a claim added, dropped, weakened, strengthened or reversed is. The check verifies the string is non-empty and nothing more — “states what is not drift as well as what is” is a reading, and a gate pretending to measure it would be the exact defect this skill exists to stop.

a78928fdae42.title: Three states, and the third is what lets it gate
a78928fdae42.content: . | verified — the adjudicator ruled. Two entries, adjudicator first. | could not dispatch — no dispatch capability was available. One entry, result: "n/a", metrics.dispatch: "unavailable", and a required reason. The producer may write this one, and only this one. | not attempted — no entry at all. | . Without state 2 the discipline cannot gate anywhere: a producer forbidden from writing a verdict has nothing to write in an environment with no subagents, so the gate reads an absence it cannot tell from negligence. Recording it keeps “could not dispatch” distinguishable from “nobody tried”. It is never a pass. isVerified() is the predicate a gate asks, and it is false for state 2 and for state 3 alike. A consumer that reads n/a as “nothing to see” turns the honest gap straight back into the silent one.

8b81cab83067.title: Recording
8b81cab83067.content: Both parties are written as witnesses. The adjudicator leads — the first entry per criterion is the operative one everywhere in this repo. The checker sits behind it with result: "n/a" and its output in notes, because a reader asking on what basis? needs the intermediate and a reader asking who did this? needs both names. Record model with model_source, or not at all. A subagent’s serving model is not observable from the session that dispatched it: it inherits the parent unless the harness overrides, and the hand-back does not say which model served the turn. A bare model string is an inference printed as a fact. Absent both, a reader gets “not recorded”, which is true and acceptable. A sweep replaces only entries whose reviewer is itself. mergeUntainted carries everything else through, so an unrelated re-run never silently deletes another party’s verdict. A human ruling is never superseded here. A verdict is hashed to what it was about. Edit the subject and the verdict goes stale. This matters more for an agent ruling than a script one, because nobody can cheaply re-run it. Where the verdict is kept: the attestation store, not the derived file . Both entries are judgements — reviewer.kind is agent (or human) — so their durable home is the attestations graph, test/attestations/<family>/<mirrored subject path>.attestations.json (qa-attestations/v1), on main. The derived test/results/ file beside them is a working copy whose record lives on the qa-reports branch, and a regeneration cannot reproduce an agent ruling. recordUntainted writes the store first, through the same resolvePrior / finalizeCriteria API as every other attesting writer, and refreshes the derived report only if one already exists — it never invents one. So the verdict lands whether or not the derived file is on the branch, and the store file it returns is the one to commit. What puts a subject in scope is the subject existing (<subject>.md or .ts), not its derived report, which does not live beside it. A corrupt or unreadable store reads UNKNOWN and is refused, with nothing written, rather than overwritten.

5311abf0ba95.title: Why the instrument is the thing to watch
5311abf0ba95.content: A measurement whose author has to explain it away is about the instrument, not the subject — for example a failure count that is really a count of entries missing from the checker’s reference map. Remove such a measurement rather than publish it. translation-manager §”The instrument, not the translation” has the worked case.

dc73c985fb9b.title: This is one rule with two homes
dc73c985fb9b.content: It is not a platform invention. Guideline methodology separates the systematic review team from the guideline development group for the same reason, and the identical rule applies to evidence-based literature review for living guidelines. When adding a domain’s rules here, run them through domain-fencing (opt-in cat-harness.kg-ops)’s three questions first: a rule that fails all three is a folio’s rule, correctly located, and fencing it and saying so is the honest move.

It deliberately does not call a model: the payload is written by whatever ran the parties, so recording works the same for two subagents, two API calls, or two people. | .

ecce6c1d1ba8.title: Upload naming — the name is normalised, not the link escaped
ecce6c1d1ba8.content: Skill upload-naming: What an ingested file may be CALLED. Read before adding anything to an uploads or library graph, before writing a generator that links to one, and before “fixing” a broken link in a generated README. Covers which characters break what, why the name is normalised as well as the link escaped, how a sidecar stays paired with its source, and the one case the fixer refuses. Named by: Content acquisition, Basic ingestion — an upload to an asset catalogued in library/, Materialize remote content: the shared subprocess, Refresh materialized remote content, Sample import into a structured data store, Subscribe to an external knowledge graph, Ingestion subprocess — ingest a theme, Theme and UI review — at ingestion, Ingestion subprocess — build the L1 knowledge graph, Ingestion subprocess — derive content from the assets, Ingestion subprocess — extract structure, Ingestion subprocess — the L1 completeness gate, Publish extracted statements with source links . A file in an uploads or library graph is named by whoever uploaded it, and that name reaches a generated Markdown link. So the name is an interface, not a label. It is a library-core skill, beside uploads-watch and library-ingestion, because what an ingested file may be called is a question about acquiring and ingesting sources. bun run cat check:upload-names reports; check:upload-names:check gates; check:upload-names:fix renames with git mv.

1acabd6b540d.title: The rule
1acabd6b540d.content: A name may not contain any of . space , ( ) [ ] { } # ? & % ' " ` < > | . Everything else is left exactly as uploaded. The fixer replaces a run of those with a single -, trims, and preserves the extension and any sidecar suffix. A name with no unsafe character is returned untouched. Collapsing and trimming happen only to names that were going to change anyway; a double dash, a leading dash or a trailing dash is not this check’s business. Case is not a defect either: README.md stays README.md, because renaming it breaks every link to it and every generator that writes one. Rewriting a name that was already safe breaks whatever looks it up by that name, such as a generator that lists a section file. Both are pinned by tests.

3f2224a43d84.title: What each character breaks
3f2224a43d84.content: | character | what it breaks | . | space, (, ) | a Markdown link target ends at the first ) | . | [ ] | the label half of the link | . | < > \| | the angle-bracket link form, and tables | . | # ? | a fragment and a query to every URL parser | . | & % quotes backtick | escaping in a shell, an href, or both | . | , | nothing — included for the stub convention | .

be9dd51fb9b6.title: Why the NAME as well as the link
be9dd51fb9b6.content: uploads/X (2).pdf produces the link target X (2).pdf, which resolves to X (2. Two layers answer this, and neither subsumes the other: . | layer | reaches | fails when | . | linkTarget (in subgraph-readmes.ts) / decodeLinkTarget (in check-subgraphs.ts) | every generated README link, in every graph typology, including directory names | never — it percent-encodes every segment of what the generator writes (parentheses included, because an unbalanced one ends a CommonMark destination as surely as a space), and the check decodes before asking the filesystem | . | this check | uploads and library names, before anything links them | a name reaches something that is not that generator | . The encoder keeps generated READMEs valid. This check keeps a filename usable in a shell, an href, a CI log line, a curl, and any later generator. Escaping is per-generator; a name is per-file, so a name that is safe everywhere is safe once. A rename churns downstream references, and that is accepted: they are repaired, not abandoned. After a rename, repoint the hand-maintained path fields (files[].path in intake.json; container and assets[].path in *.extraction.json; provenance.source in catalogue records; file and source_file in structure.json and manifest.jsonld; hardcoded paths in tests and scripts). Leave a hand-authored wireframe alone: what it depicts is a design decision, not a consequence of the rename. Then regenerate in dependency order: library:graph → library:viz → library:readmes → readme:subgraphs, then skill:register. Out of order, a later writer stales an earlier one’s output, which reads exactly like a real failure. Build the old-name list for a reference sweep from git diff --name-status -M split on tabs (awk -F'\t'), not on whitespace: the filenames being renamed contain spaces. A sweep that finds nothing must be shown to have had something to look for.

fa864e66f201.title: A sidecar suffix is not an extension
fa864e66f201.content: X.pdf pairs with X.pdf.extraction.json. Two ways to break that: . | rename the source and not the sidecar → the extraction is orphaned | normalise the sidecar by a different rule than its source → same | . So the fixer strips the sidecar suffix first, normalises the remaining name by the one rule, and restores the suffix. The pair moves together by construction. The stem is normalised and the extension left alone, because a whole-filename slug destroys the extension (…(2).pdf → …-2-pdf).

ad5fff9f1a44.title: Findings are not the size of a rename
ad5fff9f1a44.content: The check reports only what is still unnormalised, so once part of the corpus has been renamed its count is the tail of the work, not its size. Measure a rename from git diff --name-status -M.

6f678267e5b4.title: The one case it refuses
6f678267e5b4.content: Two files that normalise to one name. The fixer reports the collision and renames neither: picking a winner silently destroys an upload, and an upload is somebody’s source material. Rename one by hand. That is deletion-requires-confirmation applied to a rename — a git mv that overwrites is a deletion with a friendlier name.

10177ee7d8e6.title: What this does NOT cover
10177ee7d8e6.content: . | Directory names. The check reads files; a directory with a space in it is not graded. | Content. It reads names and never opens a file, which is why it is harness-layer rather than folio-layer in the repo partition. | Whether a file should be there at all. That is ingestion’s question, not naming’s. | .

09f4fb58d13a.title: Two mechanisms and a persona
09f4fb58d13a.content: Skill upload-routes: How a file actually REACHES uploads/ — the two mechanisms that write bytes into a declared queue, the persona that performs one of them on somebody’s behalf, and what each writer owes that the route does not do for them. The step before intake and after acquisition. Named by: Basic ingestion — an upload to an asset catalogued in library/ . content-acquisition decides what channel a resource comes in on — a file, a link, or a description somebody gives in their own words. This skill starts one step later, where the answer was a file: what writes the bytes into the declared queue, and what does the writer owe? . It ends the moment the file is in the queue. uploads-watch notices it arrived; library-ingestion and document-intake take it from there.

6baab0b74605.title: The answer is two, not three, and the third is a persona
6baab0b74605.content: Two mechanisms write bytes: a git commit, and the forge’s web UI. A file handed to an agent in a conversation is route 1 performed by a different actor. A persona inherits every obligation of the mechanism it performs, so the question about an agent is “did the agent discharge the git route’s obligations, and what does it owe on top?” Treating it as a third route would invite a third, shorter list of obligations. What it owes on top is provenance. A commit records its own author and message; a web upload records the account that made it. Neither records “this arrived in a conversation, from this person, for this reason” — that fact exists only in the session, which is ephemeral. If the agent does not write it down when it places the file, it is gone: for the other two routes a commit exists to go back to, and for a conversation nothing does.

5e336214330a.title: Route 1 — a git commit from a working tree
5e336214330a.content: git add the file under the queue, commit, push, open a PR. A working tree is where the pre-commit hook and bun run cat gates run — if you run them. What you owe. |   |   | . | put it in the declared queue of the layer that will own it | see §”Which queue” | . | run the generators the file stales | uploads/README.md is generated and lists every file, so any addition stales it. bun run cat readme:subgraphs, then bun run cat gates for the rest | . | open a PR | so CI judges it, and so a sibling session can see the queue grew | . | record where it came from | the commit message is the only place this route has for it | . You do not owe ingestion. Placing and ingesting are different acts by different skills, and uploads-watch is explicit that a drop is somebody handing over a file, not an instruction to publish it.

57c158f10c6f.title: Route 2 — the forge’s web UI
57c158f10c6f.content: GitHub’s “Add files via upload”. Never write the URL by hand — run bun run cat-harness-tools/scripts/upload-url.ts [branch], which composes it from the declaration. The declared path uploads/ is relative to the layer, and a forge URL needs it relative to the repository. There is no working tree, so there is no pre-commit hook and no generator run. The commit is minted server-side from the bytes you selected and nothing else. Two hazards: . | It commits to the path you are LOOKING at. A file outside the declared queue reads as absent to every consumer, because each resolves the queue from the declaration. | It lets you commit to any branch, including the default one. A commit straight to main skips the PR, which is the only place CI would have run: no hook locally and no CI remotely. The generated uploads/README.md is then stale on the default branch, and readme:subgraphs:check — a blocking gate — fails for whoever opens the next pull request. | . What you owe. Everything route 1 owes, discharged afterwards from a checkout, because the web UI cannot discharge any of it: . | choose the branch, not main, unless you are also going to run the generators immediately; | navigate to the declared queue directory before uploading, not to the repository root; | pull, run bun run cat readme:subgraphs and bun run cat gates, and push the result — or ask an agent to, which is the persona below. | .

ca225ab064e1.title: The persona — a file handed to an agent in a conversation
ca225ab064e1.content: This is route 1, performed by an agent. It inherits every obligation above. Three things are the agent’s own: . Materialise the bytes before anything else. A file that exists only in the conversation exists nowhere the repository can see. Write it into the declared queue under a name that will still mean something — not ChatGPT Image Sep 20, 2026, 08_26_47 AM.png or a bare UUID. Write down what the conversation knows and the commit does not — who provided it, when, what they said it was, and why it was wanted. Put it in the commit message at minimum. This is the obligation the other two routes do not have, and the reason the persona is named although it is not a mechanism. Do not ingest on your own say-so, and do not delete. Both are other skills’ decisions — library-ingestion and deletion-requires-confirmation. A processed upload still looks spent and still is not.

7e9fd36f5d56.title: What the routes are NOT responsible for
7e9fd36f5d56.content: The same three for every route, stated once so no route’s section can shorten the list: . | deciding the file belongs in the corpus. That is acquisition’s question, answered before this step. | ingestion. A file in the queue is a file in the queue; library/ is a judgement call somebody else owns. | cleaning the queue. uploads/ is the raw record of what was handed over and a derived library/ entry does not replace it. | .

a1faa614d0ac.title: Which queue — there can be more than one, and they belong to different layers
a1faa614d0ac.content: A checkout that includes several layers can carry several uploads queues — for example uploads/ declared by the layer at the repository root and cat-harness/uploads/ declared by the cat-harness layer. They are not one directory declared twice: they are two layers’ queues that share an id. So “put it in uploads/” is not an instruction — it does not say whose. Resolve the queue from the declaration of the layer that will own the material, which is what queueRepoRelative in scripts/upload-url.ts does and what the upload-url Tool exposes. Pass that layer’s root; do not paste a path.

1df846c6db3b.title: Unsettled
1df846c6db3b.content: . | Which layer owns a given file. Nothing states the rule for choosing between two declared queues. Ask, or follow whatever the surrounding work already uses. | Whether an arrival without an intake record should be refused. A gate would fail main on arrival, which is the opposite of accepting what somebody offers (content-acquisition). Whether the record is owed by the placer or minted by intake is undecided. | .

7fa04b4c449b.title: Watching the queue
7fa04b4c449b.content: Skill uploads-watch: Notice what has landed in the acquisition queue, and tell an arrival from a backlog. Reports; it never deletes, and never ingests on its own say-so. Named by: Content acquisition . uploads/ is the acquisition queue — content-acquisition puts things in it, library-ingestion takes them out. This is the step between: seeing that something arrived. The queue path is read from the declaration, never written down. It is uploads/ relative to the layer, which is not where a repository-relative consumer would look. queueRepoRelative in scripts/upload-url.ts is the one place that arithmetic lives.

c3abcfbc1735.title: An arrival is not a backlog
c3abcfbc1735.content: A file sitting in the queue says nothing on its own: it may have landed a minute ago or been waiting since before this session. Do not report a queue’s contents as news: a watcher that does becomes noise that gets ignored, and an ignored watcher reads as coverage. So report against a mark: what was there when this session began, or when the watch last ran. What is new since the mark is an arrival. Everything else is the backlog, and the backlog is mentioned once, as a count. A backlog is still a finding. A queue that has held the same file for weeks means acquisition happened and ingestion did not, and nobody noticed. That is worth one line — not silence, and not a repeated alarm.

19ee72e4b524.title: It reports; it does not act
19ee72e4b524.content: Never ingest on a watcher’s say-so. A drop is somebody handing over a file, not an instruction to publish it: ingestion decides a bib slug, writes into library/, and is a judgement call that library-ingestion owns. Never delete anything from the queue — that is deletion-requires-confirmation applied where it is most tempting, because a processed file looks spent. It is not: uploads/ is the raw record of what was handed over, and the derived entry in library/ is not a substitute for it. Report what could go, with sizes and ages, and wait to be told.

42a7770b2c62.title: What to say when something arrived
42a7770b2c62.content: Name the file, say when it landed, say what it appears to be — and then say the next step is ingestion and whether you are taking it. An arrival reported without a next step hands the reader a fact and a chore.

87e8771ca8c0.title: What to say when nothing did
87e8771ca8c0.content: Nothing, unless you were asked. A watch that reports every quiet interval trains its reader to skip it, including the round that matters.

65f4abccaef2.title: uploads-watch (skill)

490743282481.title: Adopting an upstream version bump
490743282481.content: Skill upstream-version-adoption: Watch a pinned upstream dependency for a new release, and take a candidate version through impact analysis, an MVP build, review and a person’s adopt/hold/decline decision. Reusable per pin — the theme is the first tenant, not the only one. Named by: Human Translation Workflow, Adopt a methodology from a source document, Translation review and adjudication, Translation Workflow, Copy a knowledge-graph asset into a folio, A sub-graph wants to leave, Authorise the extraction, Cut over to the separated graph, Move the graph into its repositories, Prepare a graph to stand alone, A knowledge graph leaves for its own repositories, KG to public portal, Remote-mount a dependency, Mount a declared subgraph, Build and publish a per-slice SQLite file, A sub-KG is staged in place, then leaves for its own repository, Actor and role administration, Ask the person, CRDM close-out, CRDM data model, CRDM Phase 6 — implement, MVP, acceptance, CRDM — link the work to an issue, CRDM Phase 1 — needs, CRDM Phases 2–4 — BPA and requirements, CRDM requirements, CRDM Phase 5 — beans and sign-off, Hand back to the discussion, Related work: find, sort, summarize, ask to coordinate, Render a Knowledge Graph to a CDN, Secure agent permissions, Session state machine, Publish an ArchiMate model — every picture derived from it, A harness’s default rendering, Render log — the publish branch keeps its own history, Publish a web app — declared, translated, built at its own route, Wireframe design review, Contributor feedback on a working draft, Review and publish a folio, Record agent step, Review-log watch, Is AtomicMass.lean still in sync with its data table?, Publish a folio’s Lean render with the harness chrome . An unpinned dependency is an unreviewed commit from a stranger, merged on every build. A pinned one is a commitment that somebody has to revisit. This skill is the second half: what happens between upstream cut a release and we are running it. It implements two diagrams, and the diagram is the source of truth for ordering: . | Diagram | What it is | . | upstream-pin-watch.bpmn (opt-in cat-harness.sdlc) | The watcher. Scheduled, mechanical, ends at either “every pin is current” or “one tracking issue says which is not”. | . | upstream-version-adoption.bpmn (opt-in cat-harness.sdlc) | The reusable subprocess, entered once per stale pin. Scope → impact → MVP → review → decide. | . The second is called, not copied: calledElement="Process_UpstreamAdoption". Any pinned upstream dependency enters it the same way, and a new tenant is a registry row plus a call activity — never a second diagram that says the same thing in different words.

8557edb8fb9c.title: The registry is the tenant list, and it does not hold the version
8557edb8fb9c.content: upstream/upstream-pins.json — in this harness’s declared upstream/ directory — declares each pinned dependency, with each pinnedIn resolved against the harness root: the upstream repo, the file the pin literal actually lives in, the pattern that reads it, what of ours binds to it, and the commands that constitute its MVP. It deliberately does not store the pinned version. The version lives in exactly one place — site-chrome/_config.yml for the theme — and the registry says how to read it from there. A registry that carried its own copy would be a second answer to “what are we running”, free to disagree with the build. bun run cat check:upstream-pins reads the literal out of the declared file; a pattern that matches nothing is reported as an error, not as “no pin”. binds and mvp are the reason the registry exists at all rather than the check simply grepping for version strings. They are what turn impact analysis and MVP from words in a box into a list somebody can work through.

0e1f124092cb.title: 1 — Watch
0e1f124092cb.content: bun run cat check:upstream-pins, weekly from .github/workflows/upstream-pins.yml and on demand. For each row: read the pinned ref out of its declared file, list the upstream tags that match tagPattern, and compare. Exit codes, and the middle one is the point: . | Exit | Meaning | What the workflow does | . | 0 | every pin is at the newest matching release | closes the tracking issue if one is open | . | 1 | at least one pin is behind | opens one issue labelled upstream-pin, or edits the existing one | . | 2 | could not determine — upstream unreachable, pattern did not match | leaves the issue untouched and fails the job | . Three rules it inherits from check-ci-health.ts, and they are not optional: . | “Could not check” is never rendered as current. An unreachable upstream is exit 2, not exit 0. A watchdog that goes blind must not read as good news. | One issue, edited in place. An edit does not notify, so a pin that stays stale for months stays one unread item rather than many. | The job fails on exit 2, which makes this workflow itself red on the default branch, which check:ci-health reports. The watchdog is watched. | .

37d3b5dce311.title: 2 — Impact analysis
37d3b5dce311.content: Scope the delta first, and scope it to what reaches our output. The upstream changelog is the claim; the diff is the evidence. For a Jekyll theme that means _sass, _includes, _layouts and assets — a change to upstream’s own docs, CI or tests cannot reach us: . git -C <upstream-clone> diff --stat <pinned>..<candidate> -- _sass _includes _layouts assets . Then ask what of ours binds to it, from the row’s binds list. This is the half that a changelog cannot tell you, because upstream does not know what you reached into. For the theme it is concrete and small: site-chrome/assets/js/docs-ui.js moves the theme’s own search markup into the action launcher, binding .search, #search-input and .search-label; site-chrome/assets/css/docs-ui.css overrides .side-bar, .site-header and .main-header; and three e2e specs assert the structure the theme emits. An upstream rename of any of those is not a build failure — it is a shipped feature that quietly stops working, which is the failure mode a pin exists to convert into a decision. Write the analysis down as the work item’s note before building anything. A candidate that touches nothing we bind to is a different conversation from one that renames a selector we depend on, and the reviewer needs to know which they are looking at before they look.

1c64bb0522eb.title: 3 — MVP
1c64bb0522eb.content: An MVP is a deployed build, not a description of one. Move the pin on a branch, let feature-staging.yml publish it under branches/<branch-slug>/, and run the row’s mvp commands. For the theme: . rm -rf _kg _site bun test # unit tests CI=1 bun run cat test:e2e # a11y, action tiles, sidebar panels, qa panel bun run cat-harness-tools/scripts/site-links.ts --site ./_site # every navbar tile resolves in the BUILT site . site-links.ts checks the tiles against the real _site rather than against the attribute, which is what catches a tile that 404s. A red gate is evidence, not an exit. It does not end the process and it does not loop on its own — it goes to the reviewer with everything else, because “this version breaks us” is a finding the decider needs, not a reason to stop before they see it.

646ad632a8ff.title: 4 — Review
646ad632a8ff.content: Post the staging URL, the gate results and the impact analysis on the PR, then hand it over. The reviewer’s question is narrower than “is the new version good”: it is does anything in binds still hold, checked against the deployed page rather than against a screenshot. Findings the agent can fix — our overlay adapting to a renamed class, a test fixture updated to the markup the theme now emits — loop back into impact analysis on the same branch. Findings that are upstream’s behaviour rather than ours go to the decision as they are.

188c05aae075.title: 5 — Decide
188c05aae075.content: A person decides, and the diagram says so. PM_Decide is a bpmn:userTask in the publication manager’s lane, and that role admits person only, so activity-fulfilment-kind fails the moment somebody tries to make an agent the accepting party. It also carries <cat-harness.processes:policy relaxable="false"/>: no package may relax it. The lane is the publication manager’s rather than the editor’s because the pin is not a change to the corpus — it is a change to what the published artefact is built from, and that role is the one “accountable for what is live”. The gateway is not DMN-backed, and that is deliberate. Every other computed gateway in this repository reduces to arithmetic over tool output; this one weighs a rendering nobody can score against the cost of staying behind. A table here would look authoritative and would not be. Three outcomes: . | Adopt — move the pin, open the PR, and say in the body what the version range changed in rendered output. Record the evidence you used, not just the verdict. | Hold — record it as a block with an expiry and a revisit trigger (bean-blocking.md (opt-in cat-harness.work-plan)). A hold with no expiry cannot be told from abandoned work, and the next watcher run will re-raise the same pin with no memory of why it was left. | Decline — record the reasons on the work item and scrap it. A scrapped work item is what stops the next agent re-entering the same dead end; a deleted one leaves them unable to tell a decision from an accident. | . In every case the decision is written down before the process ends. The work item is resolved from the terminal step, so a run that stops at “we looked and said no” is as finished as one that moved the pin.

c8c494424bd9.title: Adding a tenant
c8c494424bd9.content: . | Pin the literal wherever the tool reads it, with a comment saying which process governs moving it. | Add a row to upstream-pins.json: repo, pinnedIn, pattern, tagPattern, binds, mvp. | Run bun run cat check:upstream-pins and confirm it reads your pin back. A pattern that does not match is exit 2 — “could not determine” — and the row is not watched until it does. | . No diagram changes. That is what reusable means here.

0ccda92bb5b5.title: How to pick the pinned version when you first pin something
0ccda92bb5b5.content: Pin what is running, not what is newest. Those are different changes, and doing both at once means neither is reviewable — a regression cannot be attributed to the pin or to the bump. Establish what is running by fingerprint, not by assumption. For the theme that meant finding a declaration in the deployed CSS on gh-pages (text-wrap: balance, in _sass/navigation.scss) that entered upstream after the newest release, which proved the live site was tracking the default branch rather than any tag. The newest release at or below that point is the pin, and the PR states the residual delta — one CSS declaration — rather than claiming there is none. If no fingerprint discriminates, say so and pin the newest release anyway; an unverified pin is still strictly better than an unpinned dependency, and “could not determine” written down is worth more than a confident guess.
